# Developing Modular Planters

## Setup

- JDK 25 on your `PATH`. Gradle 9.8.2 starts with JDK 17 or newer through the wrapper (`./gradlew`), and the build compiles with JDK 25, which Gradle can also download through the Foojay toolchain resolver. The Java formatter hook runs the `java` on your `PATH` and reads the code with that JDK's compiler, so it needs JDK 25.
- [just](https://just.systems) for the commands below and [prek](https://prek.j178.dev) for the pre-commit hooks: `brew install just prek`. Run `prek install` once in your clone. After that, each commit formats Java with google-java-format and Markdown, YAML and JSON with Prettier, then checks the workflows and shell scripts.
- Optional, for testing the GitHub workflows before pushing: Docker, `brew install zizmor`, and `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. `just ci` runs the Build workflow in Docker and `just ci-lint` lints the workflows.
- An IDE is optional. IntelliJ IDEA imports the project from `build.gradle`, and the `idea` plugin downloads sources and javadoc for Minecraft and NeoForge. `.editorconfig` sets Java to 2-space indents and 100 columns, matching google-java-format.

The first build downloads Minecraft, NeoForge and the dev mods, so it takes a few minutes.

## Commands

Run `just` to list the recipes. Each one wraps a Gradle task or a script in `tools/`, so `./gradlew runClient` and the rest still work without just.

| Command                 | What it does                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `just build`            | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
| `just test`             | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |
| `just gametest`         | Starts a headless server that runs the in-game tests in `src/main/java/.../gametest` and exits            |
| `just check`            | Runs the unit tests, then the in-game tests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2` and with `-PnoAppliedFlux` |
| `just client`           | Starts a dev client with the mod and the dev mods below                                                   |
| `just server`           | Starts a dev dedicated server with no GUI                                                                 |
| `just data`             | Regenerates `src/generated/resources` (recipes, loot tables, lang, models)                                |
| `just gradle-update <version>` | Upgrades the Gradle wrapper to that version |
| `just lint`             | Runs every pre-commit hook on every file                                                                  |
| `just fmt`              | Formats the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place                                                  |
| `just ci-lint` | Lints the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor |
| `just ci` | Runs the Build workflow locally in Docker with local-ci, uncommitted changes included |
| `just logo`             | Redraws the logo from the block textures                                                                  |
| `just compress <files>` | Compresses PNG screenshots with pngquant and oxipng                                                       |
| `just changelog <tag>`  | Prints the changelog notes for one release                                                                |
| `just release-check`    | Checks that the version is ready to tag, then dry-runs the publish                                        |

Run `just check` and `just lint` before opening a pull request. After changing anything in `datagen`, also run `just data` and commit the result. The Build workflow runs all of these on every push and pull request, and fails if `runData` would change `src/generated`.

## Where things live

- `src/main/java`: the mod. The `gametest` and `datagen` packages are left out of the jar.
- `src/generated/resources`: output of `runData`. It is committed, so run `runData` and commit the result after changing anything in `datagen`.
- `wiki/`: the guide's pages. `processResources` copies them into the jar, where Oracle Index reads them as a book.
- `docs/description.md` and `docs/media/`: the CurseForge and Modrinth page and its images. World shots are JPEG. Screenshots of screens are PNG, compressed with `just compress <files>`, which runs `pngquant` and then `oxipng` (`brew install pngquant oxipng`). The logo PNGs are left as `tools/render_logo.py` writes them.
- `tools/changelog-section.sh`, `tools/check-release.sh` and `tools/release-version.sh`: the release checks that `just release-check` and the Release workflow run.
- `.github/workflows/`: `build.yml` runs `checks.yml` on every push and pull request, and `release.yml` runs it on a release tag before publishing.
- `tools/render_logo.py`: draws the logo from the block textures. Run `just logo` after changing a block texture, and commit both `docs/media/logo.png` and `src/main/resources/logo.png`.

## Dev mods

These are on the dev runtime (`runClient`, `runServer`, `runGameTestServer`) but not in the jar. Agritech: Evolved is the only required dependency. Each switch below leaves a mod out of a run, for example `just client -PnoAe2`.

| Mod                | Version       | Comes with                     | Switch                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Agritech: Evolved  | 2.2.0.6       |                                | required                                   |
| Jade               | 26.1.12       |                                | `-PnoJade`                                 |
| AE2                | 26.1.13-beta  | GuideME 26.1.15-beta           | `-PnoAe2`                                  |
| Applied Flux       | 26.1-1.0.2    | Glodium 26.1-1.2               | `-PnoAppliedFlux`, also off with `-PnoAe2` |
| Powah              | 7.0.4-alpha   | Cloth Config 26.1.154, GuideME | `-PnoPowah`                                |
| Oracle Index       | 2.0.0         | Architectury 20.1.17           | `-PnoOracleIndex`                          |
| Logistics Networks | 26.1.2-1.13.0 |                                | `-PnoLogisticsNetworks`                    |

The mod has code only for Jade, AE2 and Applied Flux. Powah is there for its fast FE source and cables. Oracle Index shows the guide, and Logistics Networks lets you test a node on the core. Most versions match the ones the All the Mods 11 modpack runs. Applied Flux isn't in that pack, and its AE2 build can differ.

## Releasing

A release tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0` or `26.3-0.2.0`. Pushing one runs the Release workflow. It checks the tag and runs the same checks as every push. Then it makes a GitHub release with the jar those checks built, and after that uploads the same jar to CurseForge and Modrinth.

1. Set `mod_version` in `gradle.properties` to three numbers, such as `0.2.0`. A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix, such as `0.2.0-beta`, publishes an alpha or a beta. Without one it is a full release.
2. Add a `## <tag>` section to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, below the intro line. Its notes become the release notes on all three sites.
3. Run `just release-check`. It builds the tag from `gradle.properties`, fails if the tag has the wrong format or the changelog has no notes for it, then dry-runs the publish.
4. Commit, then run `git tag <tag> && git push origin main <tag>`.

The workflow reads the repository secrets `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`, and the project ids `curseforge_project_id` and `modrinth_project_id` in `gradle.properties`. An empty id skips that site, and the run logs a notice saying so. The GitHub release uses the workflow's own token.

If an upload fails, for example because a site is down, use "Re-run failed jobs" on that workflow run. A fix that needs a code change is released as a new version with a new tag. A tag that was pushed is never moved.

## Screenshots with Structure Lab

`-PstructureLabJar=<path to jar>` adds Structure Lab to a dev run. It places a structure file in a flat world and saves screenshots from set camera angles, which is how the world shots in `docs/media/` were taken. It is a local build that isn't published, so leave the switch out unless you have the jar. It needs a world created with the "Structure Lab" world type.

input.command:
cd /Users/sweetjp/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters && gh run list --branch main --limit 3 --json conclusion,headSha,displayTitle 2>&1 | head; cat > .github/workflows/zz-localci-diag.yml <<'EOF'
name: Diag
on: push
jobs:
  diag:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: |
          git status --short src/generated | head -3
          git diff --stat src/generated | tail -3
          git diff --summary src/generated | head -5
          git diff src/generated/resources/data/modular_planters/recipe/core.json | cat -A | head -30
          git config -l | head -20
          ls -l src/generated/resources/data/modular_planters/recipe/core.json
EOF
AI_AGENT=1 local-ci run --workflow .github/workflows/zz-localci-diag.yml -q 2>&1 | tail -5; ls -t "$HOME/Library/Application Support/local-ci/logs" | head -2

lines: Run `just` to list the recipes. Each one wraps a Gradle task or a script in `tools/`, so `./gradlew runClient` and the rest still work without just.
-| `just build`            | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
-| `just test`             | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |
-| `just gametest`         | Starts a headless server that runs the in-game tests in `src/main/java/.../gametest` and exits            |
-| `just check`            | Runs the unit tests, then the in-game tests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2` and with `-PnoAppliedFlux` |
-| `just client`           | Starts a dev client with the mod and the dev mods below                                                   |
-| `just server`           | Starts a dev dedicated server with no GUI                                                                 |
-| `just data`             | Regenerates `src/generated/resources` (recipes, loot tables, lang, models)                                |
-| `just gradle-update <version>` | Upgrades the Gradle wrapper to that version |
-| `just lint`             | Runs every pre-commit hook on every file                                                                  |
-| `just fmt`              | Formats the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place                                                  |
-| `just ci-lint` | Lints the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor |
-| `just ci` | Runs the Build workflow locally in Docker with local-ci, uncommitted changes included |
-| `just logo`             | Redraws the logo from the block textures                                                                  |
-| `just compress <files>` | Compresses PNG screenshots with pngquant and oxipng                                                       |
-| `just changelog <tag>`  | Prints the changelog notes for one release                                                                |
-| `just release-check`    | Checks that the version is ready to tag, then dry-runs the publish                                        |
+| `just build`                   | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
+| `just test`                    | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |

toolUseResult.originalFile:
What replaces `glci` now that the repos are on GitHub: which local tools run, draw, and lint GitHub Actions workflows, how they were installed on this Mac, and where each one differs from a real GitHub run. Written 2026-10-31 on macOS 27 (arm64) with Docker Desktop 29.9.2, wrkflw 0.8.0, actrun 0.32.0, local-ci 0.18.1 and zizmor 1.31.1. Every behaviour under "Smoke test" was observed on a throwaway repo in `~/tmp/2026-10-31-gha-local-tools/repo`. See [[CI-CD MOC]] for the GitLab notes these replace.

## glci to GitHub, command by command

| glci | GitHub replacement |
|---|---|
| `glci run` | `wrkflw run --runtime docker <workflow>`, `actrun workflow run <workflow>`, or `local-ci run --workflow <workflow>` |
| `glci run --simulate` | `actrun workflow run <workflow> --dry-run` |
| `glci show` | `actrun viz <workflow>` (ASCII), `--mermaid`, or `--svg` |
| `glci jobs` | `wrkflw list`, or the job list in `actrun ... --dry-run` |
| `glci lint` | `actrun lint`, `wrkflw validate`, and `zizmor --offline .github/workflows` |
| `glci run --env K=V` | `local-ci run --var K=V` (or `--var-file`), or `actrun workflow run --env <file>`. wrkflw has no flag for variables |
| `glci show --context merge_request` | `actrun workflow run --trigger pull_request`, `wrkflw run --event pull_request`, or `actrun --event <payload.json>` |
| `glci run --input k=v` | `actrun workflow run --input k=v` (`workflow_dispatch` inputs) |
| `glci variables` | No equivalent. Nothing resolves `vars`, `secrets` and `if:` offline and prints the trace |
| `glab ci lint` (server render) | No equivalent. GitHub has no lint endpoint, so push a branch and use `gh workflow run` plus `gh run watch` |

wrkflw also reads `.gitlab-ci.yml` (`wrkflw validate --gitlab`, `wrkflw run --gitlab`), so it covers the odd GitLab repo too.

## Install

- `brew install wrkflw zizmor`. Both are Rust.
- `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. actrun is MoonBit compiled to JavaScript, and local-ci is TypeScript. Both need Node, which Homebrew provides.

`XDG_CACHE_HOME` makes bun put global installs in `~/.cache/.bun/bin`, which no shell has on PATH. `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` moves them to `~/.bun/install/global` with binaries in `~/.bun/bin`. `~/.bun/bin` is on PATH in fish (`conf.d/00-path.fish`) and in zsh (`~/.shell/paths.zsh`), and Claude Code's Bash tool inherits the zsh PATH from the next session on.

Three install traps:

- **actrun's curl installer is stale.** It downloads `actrun-macos-arm64.tar.gz`, but native binaries stop at v0.29.0 (2026-03-31). v0.32.0 ships only as the npm package.
- **`oda251/actrun` is the wrong repo.** It is archived and empty. The project is `mizchi/actrun`.
- **The blocked protobufjs postinstall is fine.** bun blocks it for local-ci's dependency tree, and the script only prints a version-scheme warning.

## Smoke test

The test workflow had a two-entry `build` matrix that runs `actions/checkout`, and a `test` job that `needs: build` and has **no** checkout step. On GitHub, that second job starts with an empty workspace, so its `test -f .github/workflows/ci.yml` fails.

| Tool and mode | Where steps ran | `test` job (no checkout) | Matches GitHub? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wrkflw run --runtime docker` | `ubuntu:latest` container | failed | yes |
| `actrun workflow run --workspace-mode worktree` | the Mac itself (`uname` printed `Darwin arm64`) | passed | no |
| `local-ci run` | `ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner` container (`Linux aarch64`) | passed | no |

So actrun and local-ci both hand the working tree to every job, and a job that forgot its checkout passes locally and fails on GitHub. Only wrkflw caught that.

## Picking a runner

- **wrkflw, Docker runtime:** the most faithful workspace model of the three, for workflows made of `run:` steps. Its default image is bare `ubuntu:latest`, so tools a GitHub runner has (node, python, gh) are missing unless a job installs them. `--preserve-containers-on-failure` keeps the container for poking at. The README's `wrkflw run --jobs` flag does not exist in 0.8.0. Use `wrkflw list` and `--job <name>`. Three more traps in 0.8.0, seen on 2026-11-04:
  - There is no `-P` flag for mapping `ubuntu-latest` to a fuller image.
  - With Docker Desktop running, it can print "Docker not available, falling back to emulation mode" and then run the steps on the Mac. Prefix the command with `DOCKER_HOST="$(docker context inspect --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}')"`.
  - It runs each JavaScript action (for example `oven-sh/setup-bun`) in its own `node:24-slim` container, so whatever a `setup-*` action installs is gone by the next `run:` step. A workflow that relies on one fails with "command not found".
- **local-ci:** runs GitHub's own runner binary against a local copy of the API, so `actions/checkout`, `actions/cache` and artifacts behave as they do on GitHub. `-p` pauses on a failed step and leaves the container up. Fix the file, then `local-ci retry --name <runner>` (`--from-step N` to skip ahead). It needs a GitHub remote or `GITHUB_REPO=owner/repo`. The first run pulls a ~417 MB runner image. Containers are arm64 on Apple Silicon, while GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` is x64. Logs go to `~/Library/Application Support/local-ci/logs/<runner>/steps/`. Three traps in 0.18.1, seen on 2026-11-04:
  - It replaces `git fetch` in the container with a no-op ("[Local CI Shim] Intercepted 'fetch'"), so any step that clones another repo fails. `j178/prek-action` fails with "Failed to clone repo ... pathspec 'v0.9.3' did not match", even though the tag exists.
  - `lycheeverse/lychee-action` fails with "install: setting permissions for '/home/runner/_work/_temp/lychee/bin/lychee': Operation not permitted".
  - `-p` only pauses `run:` steps. A failed `uses:` step ends the job, so there is nothing to `retry`.
  To test the steps after a broken action, run a temporary copy of the workflow with that step deleted. `--workflow` reads the file from the working tree, so the copy needs no commit.
- **actrun:** the `gh`-style interface (`actrun run list/view/logs`), `--dry-run` plans, `viz`, and the best expression lint. Its default is to run steps on the Mac, which is a different kind of tool from glci, as the next section explains.

## actrun runs on the Mac, not in a container

glci ran every job in Docker. actrun's default `workspace_mode` is `local`: the workflow's commands run in the current folder with the Mac's own tools and credentials. A workflow that deletes files, installs software, or publishes a release does that for real. `actrun init` also writes `trust_actions = true`, which runs third-party actions without asking.

- Run `--dry-run` first.
- Use `--workspace-mode worktree` for a separate checkout, or `--workspace-mode docker` for container isolation. Worktree mode isolates files, not the OS: steps still run on macOS.
- Set `trust_actions = false` in any `actrun.toml`.
- Each run leaves an untracked `_build/` in the repo, and worktree mode also leaves a registered git worktree under `_build/actrun/workspace/`. Add `_build/` to `.gitignore`, and run `git worktree prune` after deleting it.

## Linting

On the test workflow, which had `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` inside a `run:` block:

- `wrkflw validate` said `Valid`. It checks the schema only.
- `actrun lint` flagged `script-injection`. It also type-checks expressions, `needs` cycles, step references, and dead `if:` branches. `--preset strict` adds rules such as `missing-timeout`.
- `zizmor --offline .github/workflows` flagged the injection (with an auto-fix) and `unpinned-uses` on `actions/checkout@v4`. Dropping `--offline` lets it make audits that call the GitHub API.

Not installed, and the fallback if these fall short: `actionlint` (Go), which also runs shellcheck over `run:` blocks, and `act` (Go, `brew install act`), the most widely used local runner.

The CI step is done. local-ci passed the `build` job and all three `gametest` jobs on v6.4.1 with `cache-provider: basic`. Two other jobs failed under local-ci, both because of local-ci itself (details below), and I couldn't confirm locally that the cache restores. Nothing is committed.

**What changed**
- **Workflows:** all six `setup-gradle` uses are now pinned to `8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1` with `cache-provider: basic`. The setup-gradle logs confirm "This build uses the basic open-source caching provider".
- **`justfile`:**
  - `just ci` runs the Build workflow in local-ci, uncommitted changes included. It checks that Docker is running first.
  - `just ci-lint` runs `actrun lint` and `zizmor`.
  - A private `require` recipe now runs before every recipe that uses an outside tool (`prek`, `uv`, `pngquant`/`oxipng`, `actrun`/`zizmor`, `local-ci`/`docker`). When a tool is missing it stops with `error: missing <tool>. See the Setup section of DEVELOPMENT.md.` I tested that with fake tool names.
- **`DEVELOPMENT.md`:** the Setup section now covers the optional tools, the new recipes are in the table, and `just fmt` realigned the table.

**Results**
- **Linters:** `actrun lint` and `zizmor` report exactly the same findings on HEAD and on the edited workflows, so the edit added none. `just lint` passes.
- **local-ci on the Build workflow:**
  - Passed: `build` and `gametest` with no flag, `-PnoAe2` and `-PnoAppliedFlux`.
  - `prek` failed: local-ci's git shim breaks the hook clone, as the runbook predicts.
  - `generated-data` failed: local-ci checks every file out with mode `rwxrwxrwx`. Git then lists all 46 generated files as modified with zero content changes. Your local `runData` leaves no diff.
- **Cache:** with `cache-read-only: false` in a temporary copy, each of two runs saved the cache (about 540 MB) under the same key. The second run still found nothing to restore, so whether the cache restores can only be confirmed on GitHub.
- **Removed:** the temporary diagnostic and cache-test workflows.

**Decisions for you**
1. **`just ci-lint` always fails right now.** zizmor exits 14 on 22 high and 10 low findings that already existed: 19 `unpinned-uses`, 3 `cache-poisoning` on `setup-gradle` in the release jobs, plus `artipacked` and `self-repository`. You can fix them separately, or make zizmor report without failing. Which do you want?
2. **`just ci` always shows the two failures above.** Changing the `generated-data` check to `git -c core.fileMode=false status --porcelain src/generated` would fix the second one and works the same on GitHub. The `prek` failure would still be there. Should I make that change?

**Other notes**
- `git diff` shows `gradlew.bat` as fully rewritten. The new wrapper writes it with CRLF line endings, and your git config converts it to LF when you commit, so most of that diff disappears.
- I added the three local-ci findings (the file mode, the read-only cache, and the cache not carrying over between runs) to your runbook, `Running GitHub Actions workflows locally.md`. I also logged two papercuts in `~/.config/papercuts.md`.

### Local CI testing (parked 2026-11-05)

The Gradle 9.8.2 and setup-gradle v6.4.1 upgrade added `just ci` (runs the Build workflow in Docker with local-ci) and `just ci-lint` (actrun and zizmor). Both work, but neither ends green yet:

1. **`just ci-lint` always fails.** zizmor exits 14 on findings that were in the workflows before the upgrade: 19 `unpinned-uses` (the `actions/*@vN` tags), 3 `cache-poisoning` on `setup-gradle` in the release jobs, 8 `artipacked` (`actions/checkout` keeps credentials) and 2 `self-repository` (`./.github/workflows/checks.yml` could be `$/...`). Options: fix the findings, or have the recipe report them without failing. `actrun lint` only warns that the `verify` job's outputs are unused, which is wrong: `if: needs.verify.outputs...` uses them.
2. **`just ci` always shows 2 failed jobs out of 6.**
   - `generated-data`: local-ci checks files out with mode `rwxrwxrwx`, so `git status` lists all 46 generated files as changed with no content change. Changing the check to `git -c core.fileMode=false status --porcelain src/generated` fixes it locally and behaves the same on GitHub.
   - `prek`: local-ci replaces `git fetch` in the container, so `j178/prek-action` cannot clone the hook repos. No fix in this repo; run `just lint` instead.

What replaces `glci` now that the repos are on GitHub: which local tools run, draw, and lint GitHub Actions workflows, how they were installed on this Mac, and where each one differs from a real GitHub run. Written 2026-10-31 on macOS 27 (arm64) with Docker Desktop 29.9.2, wrkflw 0.8.0, actrun 0.32.0, local-ci 0.18.1 and zizmor 1.31.1. Every behaviour under "Smoke test" was observed on a throwaway repo in `~/tmp/2026-10-31-gha-local-tools/repo`. See [[CI-CD MOC]] for the GitLab notes these replace.

## glci to GitHub, command by command

| glci | GitHub replacement |
|---|---|
| `glci run` | `wrkflw run --runtime docker <workflow>`, `actrun workflow run <workflow>`, or `local-ci run --workflow <workflow>` |
| `glci run --simulate` | `actrun workflow run <workflow> --dry-run` |
| `glci show` | `actrun viz <workflow>` (ASCII), `--mermaid`, or `--svg` |
| `glci jobs` | `wrkflw list`, or the job list in `actrun ... --dry-run` |
| `glci lint` | `actrun lint`, `wrkflw validate`, and `zizmor --offline .github/workflows` |
| `glci run --env K=V` | `local-ci run --var K=V` (or `--var-file`), or `actrun workflow run --env <file>`. wrkflw has no flag for variables |
| `glci show --context merge_request` | `actrun workflow run --trigger pull_request`, `wrkflw run --event pull_request`, or `actrun --event <payload.json>` |
| `glci run --input k=v` | `actrun workflow run --input k=v` (`workflow_dispatch` inputs) |
| `glci variables` | No equivalent. Nothing resolves `vars`, `secrets` and `if:` offline and prints the trace |
| `glab ci lint` (server render) | No equivalent. GitHub has no lint endpoint, so push a branch and use `gh workflow run` plus `gh run watch` |

wrkflw also reads `.gitlab-ci.yml` (`wrkflw validate --gitlab`, `wrkflw run --gitlab`), so it covers the odd GitLab repo too.

## Install

- `brew install wrkflw zizmor`. Both are Rust.
- `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. actrun is MoonBit compiled to JavaScript, and local-ci is TypeScript. Both need Node, which Homebrew provides.

`XDG_CACHE_HOME` makes bun put global installs in `~/.cache/.bun/bin`, which no shell has on PATH. `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` moves them to `~/.bun/install/global` with binaries in `~/.bun/bin`. `~/.bun/bin` is on PATH in fish (`conf.d/00-path.fish`) and in zsh (`~/.shell/paths.zsh`), and Claude Code's Bash tool inherits the zsh PATH from the next session on.

Three install traps:

- **actrun's curl installer is stale.** It downloads `actrun-macos-arm64.tar.gz`, but native binaries stop at v0.29.0 (2026-03-31). v0.32.0 ships only as the npm package.
- **`oda251/actrun` is the wrong repo.** It is archived and empty. The project is `mizchi/actrun`.
- **The blocked protobufjs postinstall is fine.** bun blocks it for local-ci's dependency tree, and the script only prints a version-scheme warning.

## Smoke test

The test workflow had a two-entry `build` matrix that runs `actions/checkout`, and a `test` job that `needs: build` and has **no** checkout step. On GitHub, that second job starts with an empty workspace, so its `test -f .github/workflows/ci.yml` fails.

| Tool and mode | Where steps ran | `test` job (no checkout) | Matches GitHub? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wrkflw run --runtime docker` | `ubuntu:latest` container | failed | yes |
| `actrun workflow run --workspace-mode worktree` | the Mac itself (`uname` printed `Darwin arm64`) | passed | no |
| `local-ci run` | `ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner` container (`Linux aarch64`) | passed | no |

So actrun and local-ci both hand the working tree to every job, and a job that forgot its checkout passes locally and fails on GitHub. Only wrkflw caught that.

## Picking a runner

- **wrkflw, Docker runtime:** the most faithful workspace model of the three, for workflows made of `run:` steps. Its default image is bare `ubuntu:latest`, so tools a GitHub runner has (node, python, gh) are missing unless a job installs them. `--preserve-containers-on-failure` keeps the container for poking at. The README's `wrkflw run --jobs` flag does not exist in 0.8.0. Use `wrkflw list` and `--job <name>`. Three more traps in 0.8.0, seen on 2026-11-04:
  - There is no `-P` flag for mapping `ubuntu-latest` to a fuller image.
  - With Docker Desktop running, it can print "Docker not available, falling back to emulation mode" and then run the steps on the Mac. Prefix the command with `DOCKER_HOST="$(docker context inspect --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}')"`.
  - It runs each JavaScript action (for example `oven-sh/setup-bun`) in its own `node:24-slim` container, so whatever a `setup-*` action installs is gone by the next `run:` step. A workflow that relies on one fails with "command not found".
- **local-ci:** runs GitHub's own runner binary against a local copy of the API, so `actions/checkout`, `actions/cache` and artifacts behave as they do on GitHub. `-p` pauses on a failed step and leaves the container up. Fix the file, then `local-ci retry --name <runner>` (`--from-step N` to skip ahead). It needs a GitHub remote or `GITHUB_REPO=owner/repo`. The first run pulls a ~417 MB runner image. Containers are arm64 on Apple Silicon, while GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` is x64. Logs go to `~/Library/Application Support/local-ci/logs/<runner>/steps/`. Three traps in 0.18.1, seen on 2026-11-04:
  - It replaces `git fetch` in the container with a no-op ("[Local CI Shim] Intercepted 'fetch'"), so any step that clones another repo fails. `j178/prek-action` fails with "Failed to clone repo ... pathspec 'v0.9.3' did not match", even though the tag exists.
  - `lycheeverse/lychee-action` fails with "install: setting permissions for '/home/runner/_work/_temp/lychee/bin/lychee': Operation not permitted".
  - `-p` only pauses `run:` steps. A failed `uses:` step ends the job, so there is nothing to `retry`.
  To test the steps after a broken action, run a temporary copy of the workflow with that step deleted. `--workflow` reads the file from the working tree, so the copy needs no commit.
  Three more traps, seen on 2026-11-05 with a Gradle mod repo:
  - Every checked-out file has mode `rwxrwxrwx`, so `git status` in the job reports each file as modified (`mode change 100644 => 100755`, no content change). A step that fails when `git status --porcelain` is not empty always fails locally and passes on GitHub.
  - `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` runs with `cache-read-only: true`, because local-ci's run does not count as the default branch. Set `cache-read-only: false` in a temporary copy to make it save.
  - Even then, a cache entry saved in one `local-ci run` was not found by the next run with the same key, so cache restores cannot be tested locally. Confirm them on GitHub.
- **actrun:** the `gh`-style interface (`actrun run list/view/logs`), `--dry-run` plans, `viz`, and the best expression lint. Its default is to run steps on the Mac, which is a different kind of tool from glci, as the next section explains.

## actrun runs on the Mac, not in a container

glci ran every job in Docker. actrun's default `workspace_mode` is `local`: the workflow's commands run in the current folder with the Mac's own tools and credentials. A workflow that deletes files, installs software, or publishes a release does that for real. `actrun init` also writes `trust_actions = true`, which runs third-party actions without asking.

- Run `--dry-run` first.
- Use `--workspace-mode worktree` for a separate checkout, or `--workspace-mode docker` for container isolation. Worktree mode isolates files, not the OS: steps still run on macOS.
- Set `trust_actions = false` in any `actrun.toml`.
- Each run leaves an untracked `_build/` in the repo, and worktree mode also leaves a registered git worktree under `_build/actrun/workspace/`. Add `_build/` to `.gitignore`, and run `git worktree prune` after deleting it.

## Linting

On the test workflow, which had `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` inside a `run:` block:

- `wrkflw validate` said `Valid`. It checks the schema only.
- `actrun lint` flagged `script-injection`. It also type-checks expressions, `needs` cycles, step references, and dead `if:` branches. `--preset strict` adds rules such as `missing-timeout`.
- `zizmor --offline .github/workflows` flagged the injection (with an auto-fix) and `unpinned-uses` on `actions/checkout@v4`. Dropping `--offline` lets it make audits that call the GitHub API.

Not installed, and the fallback if these fall short: `actionlint` (Go), which also runs shellcheck over `run:` blocks, and `act` (Go, `brew install act`), the most widely used local runner.

# Developing Modular Planters

## Setup

- JDK 25 on your `PATH`. Gradle 9.8.2 starts with JDK 17 or newer through the wrapper (`./gradlew`), and the build compiles with JDK 25, which Gradle can also download through the Foojay toolchain resolver. The Java formatter hook runs the `java` on your `PATH` and reads the code with that JDK's compiler, so it needs JDK 25.
- [just](https://just.systems) for the commands below and [prek](https://prek.j178.dev) for the pre-commit hooks: `brew install just prek`. Run `prek install` once in your clone. After that, each commit formats Java with google-java-format and Markdown, YAML and JSON with Prettier, then checks the workflows and shell scripts.
- Optional, for redrawing the logo with `just logo`: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (`brew install uv`). For compressing screenshots with `just compress`: `brew install pngquant oxipng`.
- Optional, for testing the GitHub workflows before pushing: Docker, `brew install zizmor`, and `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. `just ci` runs the Build workflow in Docker and `just ci-lint` lints the workflows.
- An IDE is optional. IntelliJ IDEA imports the project from `build.gradle`, and the `idea` plugin downloads sources and javadoc for Minecraft and NeoForge. `.editorconfig` sets Java to 2-space indents and 100 columns, matching google-java-format.

The first build downloads Minecraft, NeoForge and the dev mods, so it takes a few minutes.

## Commands

Run `just` to list the recipes. Each one wraps a Gradle task or a script in `tools/`, so `./gradlew runClient` and the rest still work without just.

| Command                        | What it does                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `just build`                   | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
| `just test`                    | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |
| `just gametest`                | Starts a headless server that runs the in-game tests in `src/main/java/.../gametest` and exits            |
| `just check`                   | Runs the unit tests, then the in-game tests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2` and with `-PnoAppliedFlux` |
| `just client`                  | Starts a dev client with the mod and the dev mods below                                                   |
| `just server`                  | Starts a dev dedicated server with no GUI                                                                 |
| `just data`                    | Regenerates `src/generated/resources` (recipes, loot tables, lang, models)                                |
| `just gradle-update <version>` | Upgrades the Gradle wrapper to that version                                                               |
| `just lint`                    | Runs every pre-commit hook on every file                                                                  |
| `just fmt`                     | Formats the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place                                                  |
| `just ci-lint`                 | Lints the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor                                                         |
| `just ci`                      | Runs the Build workflow locally in Docker with local-ci, uncommitted changes included                     |
| `just logo`                    | Redraws the logo from the block textures                                                                  |
| `just compress <files>`        | Compresses PNG screenshots with pngquant and oxipng                                                       |
| `just changelog <tag>`         | Prints the changelog notes for one release                                                                |
| `just release-check`           | Checks that the version is ready to tag, then dry-runs the publish                                        |

Run `just check` and `just lint` before opening a pull request. After changing anything in `datagen`, also run `just data` and commit the result. The Build workflow runs all of these on every push and pull request, and fails if `runData` would change `src/generated`.

## Where things live

- `src/main/java`: the mod. The `gametest` and `datagen` packages are left out of the jar.
- `src/generated/resources`: output of `runData`. It is committed, so run `runData` and commit the result after changing anything in `datagen`.
- `wiki/`: the guide's pages. `processResources` copies them into the jar, where Oracle Index reads them as a book.
- `docs/description.md` and `docs/media/`: the CurseForge and Modrinth page and its images. World shots are JPEG. Screenshots of screens are PNG, compressed with `just compress <files>`, which runs `pngquant` and then `oxipng` (`brew install pngquant oxipng`). The logo PNGs are left as `tools/render_logo.py` writes them.
- `tools/changelog-section.sh`, `tools/check-release.sh` and `tools/release-version.sh`: the release checks that `just release-check` and the Release workflow run.
- `.github/workflows/`: `build.yml` runs `checks.yml` on every push and pull request, and `release.yml` runs it on a release tag before publishing.
- `tools/render_logo.py`: draws the logo from the block textures. Run `just logo` after changing a block texture, and commit both `docs/media/logo.png` and `src/main/resources/logo.png`.

## Dev mods

These are on the dev runtime (`runClient`, `runServer`, `runGameTestServer`) but not in the jar. Agritech: Evolved is the only required dependency. Each switch below leaves a mod out of a run, for example `just client -PnoAe2`.

| Mod                | Version       | Comes with                     | Switch                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Agritech: Evolved  | 2.2.0.6       |                                | required                                   |
| Jade               | 26.1.12       |                                | `-PnoJade`                                 |
| AE2                | 26.1.13-beta  | GuideME 26.1.15-beta           | `-PnoAe2`                                  |
| Applied Flux       | 26.1-1.0.2    | Glodium 26.1-1.2               | `-PnoAppliedFlux`, also off with `-PnoAe2` |
| Powah              | 7.0.4-alpha   | Cloth Config 26.1.154, GuideME | `-PnoPowah`                                |
| Oracle Index       | 2.0.0         | Architectury 20.1.17           | `-PnoOracleIndex`                          |
| Logistics Networks | 26.1.2-1.13.0 |                                | `-PnoLogisticsNetworks`                    |

The mod has code only for Jade, AE2 and Applied Flux. Powah is there for its fast FE source and cables. Oracle Index shows the guide, and Logistics Networks lets you test a node on the core. Most versions match the ones the All the Mods 11 modpack runs. Applied Flux isn't in that pack, and its AE2 build can differ.

## Releasing

A release tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0` or `26.3-0.2.0`. Pushing one runs the Release workflow. It checks the tag and runs the same checks as every push. Then it makes a GitHub release with the jar those checks built, and after that uploads the same jar to CurseForge and Modrinth.

1. Set `mod_version` in `gradle.properties` to three numbers, such as `0.2.0`. A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix, such as `0.2.0-beta`, publishes an alpha or a beta. Without one it is a full release.
2. Add a `## <tag>` section to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, below the intro line. Its notes become the release notes on all three sites.
3. Run `just release-check`. It builds the tag from `gradle.properties`, fails if the tag has the wrong format or the changelog has no notes for it, then dry-runs the publish.
4. Commit, then run `git tag <tag> && git push origin main <tag>`.

The workflow reads the repository secrets `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`, and the project ids `curseforge_project_id` and `modrinth_project_id` in `gradle.properties`. An empty id skips that site, and the run logs a notice saying so. The GitHub release uses the workflow's own token.

If an upload fails, for example because a site is down, use "Re-run failed jobs" on that workflow run. A fix that needs a code change is released as a new version with a new tag. A tag that was pushed is never moved.

## Screenshots with Structure Lab

`-PstructureLabJar=<path to jar>` adds Structure Lab to a dev run. It places a structure file in a flat world and saves screenshots from set camera angles, which is how the world shots in `docs/media/` were taken. It is a local build that isn't published, so leave the switch out unless you have the jar. It needs a world created with the "Structure Lab" world type.

Gradle 9.8.2 starts with JDK 17 or newer through the wrapper (`./gradlew`), and the build compiles with JDK 25, which Gradle can also download through the Foojay toolchain resolver. The Java formatter hook runs the `java` on your `PATH` and reads the code with that JDK's compiler, so it needs JDK 25.
6	- [just](https://just.systems) for the commands below and [prek](https://prek.j178.dev) for the pre-commit hooks: `brew install just prek`. Run `prek install` once in your clone. After that, each commit formats Java with google-java-format and Markdown, YAML and JSON with Prettier, then checks the workflows and shell scripts.
7	- Optional, for redrawing the logo with `just logo`: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (`brew install uv`). For compressing screenshots with `just compress`: `brew install pngquant oxipng`.
8	- Optional, for testing the GitHub workflows before pushing: Docker, `brew install zizmor`, and `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. `just ci` runs the Build workflow in Docker and `just ci-lint` lints the workflows.
9	- An IDE is optional. IntelliJ IDEA imports the project from `build.gradle`, and the `idea` plugin downloads sources and javadoc for Minecraft and NeoForge. `.editorconfig` sets Java to 2-space indents and 100 columns, matching google-java-format.
10	
11	The first build downloads Minecraft, NeoForge and the dev mods, so it takes a few minutes.
12	
13	## Commands
14	
15	Run `just` to list the recipes. Each one wraps a Gradle task or a script in `tools/`, so `./gradlew runClient` and the rest still work without just.
16	
17	| Command                        | What it does                                                                                              |
18	| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
19	| `just build`                   | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
20	| `just test`                    | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |
21	| `just gametest`                | Starts a headless server that runs the in-game tests in `src/main/java/.../gametest` and exits            |
22	| `just check`                   | Runs the unit tests, then the in-game tests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2` and with `-PnoAppliedFlux` |
23	| `just client`                  | Starts a dev client with the mod and the dev mods below                                                   |
24	| `just server`                  | Starts a dev dedicated server with no GUI                                                                 |
25	| `just data`                    | Regenerates `src/generated/resources` (recipes, loot tables, lang, models)                                |
26	| `just gradle-update <version>` | Upgrades the Gradle wrapper to that version                                                               |
27	| `just lint`                    | Runs every pre-commit hook on every file                                                                  |
28	| `just fmt`                     | Formats the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place                                                  |
29	| `just ci-lint`                 | Lints the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor                                                         |
30	| `just ci`                      | Runs the Build workflow locally in Docker with local-ci, uncommitted changes included                     |
31	| `just logo`                    | Redraws the logo from the block textures                                                                  |
32	| `just compress <files>`        | Compresses PNG screenshots with pngquant and oxipng                                                       |
33	| `just changelog <tag>`         | Prints the changelog notes for one release                                                                |
34	| `just release-check`           | Checks that the version is ready to tag, then dry-runs the publish                                        |
35	
36	Run `just check` and `just lint` before opening a pull request. After changing anything in `datagen`, also run `just data` and commit the result. The Build workflow runs all of these on every push and pull request, and fails if `runData` would change `src/generated`.
37	
38	## Where things live
39	
40	- `src/main/java`: the mod. The `gametest` and `datagen` packages are left out of the jar.
41	- `src/generated/resources`: output of `runData`. It is committed, so run `runData` and commit the result after changing anything in `datagen`.
42	- `wiki/`: the guide's pages. `processResources` copies them into the jar, where Oracle Index reads them as a book.
43	- `docs/description.md` and `docs/media/`: the CurseForge and Modrinth page and its images. World shots are JPEG. Screenshots of screens are PNG, compressed with `just compress <files>`, which runs `pngquant` and then `oxipng` (`brew install pngquant oxipng`). The logo PNGs are left as `tools/render_logo.py` writes them.
44	- `tools/changelog-section.sh`, `tools/check-release.sh` and `tools/release-version.sh`: the release checks that `just release-check` and the Release workflow run.
45	- `.github/workflows/`: `build.yml` runs `checks.yml` on every push and pull request, and `release.yml` runs it on a release tag before publishing.
46	- `tools/render_logo.py`: draws the logo from the block textures. Run `just logo` after changing a block texture, and commit both `docs/media/logo.png` and `src/main/resources/logo.png`.
47	
48	## Dev mods
49	
50	These are on the dev runtime (`runClient`, `runServer`, `runGameTestServer`) but not in the jar. Agritech: Evolved is the only required dependency. Each switch below leaves a mod out of a run, for example `just client -PnoAe2`.
51	
52	| Mod                | Version       | Comes with                     | Switch                                     |
53	| ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
54	| Agritech: Evolved  | 2.2.0.6       |                                | required                                   |
55	| Jade               | 26.1.12       |                                | `-PnoJade`                                 |
56	| AE2                | 26.1.13-beta  | GuideME 26.1.15-beta           | `-PnoAe2`                                  |
57	| Applied Flux       | 26.1-1.0.2    | Glodium 26.1-1.2               | `-PnoAppliedFlux`, also off with `-PnoAe2` |
58	| Powah              | 7.0.4-alpha   | Cloth Config 26.1.154, GuideME | `-PnoPowah`                                |
59	| Oracle Index       | 2.0.0         | Architectury 20.1.17           | `-PnoOracleIndex`                          |
60	| Logistics Networks | 26.1.2-1.13.0 |                                | `-PnoLogisticsNetworks`                    |
61	
62	The mod has code only for Jade, AE2 and Applied Flux. Powah is there for its fast FE source and cables. Oracle Index shows the guide, and Logistics Networks lets you test a node on the core. Most versions match the ones the All the Mods 11 modpack runs. Applied Flux isn't in that pack, and its AE2 build can differ.
63	
64	## Releasing
65	
66	A release tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0` or `26.3-0.2.0`. Pushing one runs the Release workflow. It checks the tag and runs the same checks as every push. Then it makes a GitHub release with the jar those checks built, and after that uploads the same jar to CurseForge and Modrinth.
67	
68	1. Set `mod_version` in `gradle.properties` to three numbers, such as `0.2.0`. A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix, such as `0.2.0-beta`, publishes an alpha or a beta. Without one it is a full release.
69	2. Add a `## <tag>` section to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, below the intro line. Its notes become the release notes on all three sites.
70	3. Run `just release-check`. It builds the tag from `gradle.properties`, fails if the tag has the wrong format or the changelog has no notes for it, then dry-runs the publish.
71	4. Commit, then run `git tag <tag> && git push origin main <tag>`.
72	
73	The workflow reads the repository secrets `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`, and the project ids `curseforge_project_id` and `modrinth_project_id` in `gradle.properties`. An empty id skips that site, and the run logs a notice saying so. The GitHub release uses the workflow's own token.
74	
75	If an upload fails, for example because a site is down, use "Re-run failed jobs" on that workflow run. A fix that needs a code change is released as a new version with a new tag. A tag that was pushed is never moved.
76	
77	## Screenshots with Structure Lab
78	
79	`-PstructureLabJar=<path to jar>` adds Structure Lab to a dev run. It places a structure file in a flat world and saves screenshots from set camera angles, which is how the world shots in `docs/media/` were taken. It is a local build that isn't published, so leave the switch out unless you have the jar. It needs a world created with the "Structure Lab" world type.
80	
</system-reminder>

# Local shortcuts for building, testing, formatting and releasing Modular Planters. `just` lists them, and `just <recipe>` runs one.
#
# CI does not call just. The workflows in .github/workflows run the same Gradle tasks and tools/ scripts directly.

set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]

# Recipe arguments arrive as $1, $2 and so on, so variadic recipes forward them with "$@" and keep each argument intact.
set positional-arguments

[private]
default:
    @just --list --unsorted

# Recipes that call tools outside the JDK depend on this, so a missing tool stops the recipe before it starts. DEVELOPMENT.md says how to install each one.
[private]
require +tools:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    missing=()
    for tool in "$@"; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || missing+=("$tool")
    done
    if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "error: missing ${missing[*]}. See the Setup section of DEVELOPMENT.md." >&2
        exit 1
    fi

[doc('Compile, run the unit tests and build the jar into build/libs/')]
[group('gradle')]
build:
    ./gradlew build

[doc('Run the unit tests in src/test')]
[group('gradle')]
test:
    ./gradlew test

[doc('Run the in-game tests on a headless server, for example: just gametest -PnoAe2')]
[group('gradle')]
gametest *flags:
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer "$@"

[doc('Run the unit tests, then the in-game tests with all dev mods, without AE2 and without Applied Flux, the three ways CI runs them')]
[group('gradle')]
check:
    ./gradlew test
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer -PnoAe2
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer -PnoAppliedFlux

[doc('Start a dev client, for example: just client -PnoPowah')]
[group('gradle')]
client *flags:
    ./gradlew runClient "$@"

[doc('Start a dev dedicated server')]
[group('gradle')]
server *flags:
    ./gradlew runServer "$@"

[doc('Regenerate src/generated/resources')]
[group('gradle')]
data:
    ./gradlew runData

# The first run updates gradle-wrapper.properties with the old Gradle, and the second run lets the new Gradle rewrite gradlew and gradle-wrapper.jar to match it.
[doc('Upgrade the Gradle wrapper, for example: just gradle-update 9.8.2')]
[group('gradle')]
gradle-update version:
    ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version "$1"
    ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version "$1"

[doc('Run every pre-commit hook on every file, as CI does')]
[group('lint')]
lint: (require "prek")
    prek run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

# The formatters exit 1 when they rewrite a file, so a second run decides the result: it passes when the first run fixed everything.
[doc('Format the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place')]
[group('lint')]
fmt: (require "prek")
    prek run --all-files pretty-format-java prettier || prek run --all-files pretty-format-java prettier

[doc('Lint the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor')]
[group('ci')]
ci-lint: (require "actrun" "zizmor")
    actrun lint
    zizmor --offline .github/workflows

# local-ci runs the jobs in Docker with GitHub's own runner, against the working tree including uncommitted changes.
[doc('Run the Build workflow locally in Docker, for example: just ci -p to pause on a failed step')]
[group('ci')]
ci *flags: (require "local-ci" "docker")
    @docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop first." >&2; exit 1; }
    local-ci run --workflow .github/workflows/build.yml "$@"

[doc('Render the mod logo into docs/media/logo.png and src/main/resources/logo.png')]
[group('media')]
logo: (require "uv")
    uv run tools/render_logo.py

[doc('Compress PNG files in place, for example: just compress docs/media/*.png')]
[group('media')]
compress +files: (require "pngquant" "oxipng")
    pngquant --quality=80-95 --speed 1 --strip --force --ext .png "$@"
    oxipng -o 4 --strip safe "$@"

[doc('Print the changelog notes for one release tag, for example: just changelog 26.1.2-0.1.0')]
[group('release')]
changelog version:
    @bash tools/changelog-section.sh "$1"

[doc('Check that the version in gradle.properties is ready to tag, then dry-run the publish to GitHub, CurseForge and Modrinth')]
[group('release')]
release-check:
    bash tools/check-release.sh "$(bash tools/release-version.sh)"
    DRY_RUN=1 GITHUB_TOKEN=REDACTED ./gradlew publishMods

name: Release

# Any tag shaped like a release starts this, such as 26.1.2-0.1.0 or 26.3-0.2.0, and the verify job stops every tag that
# isn't the version in gradle.properties.
on:
  push:
    tags: ["*.*-*.*.*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      curseforge: ${{ steps.projects.outputs.curseforge }}
      modrinth: ${{ steps.projects.outputs.modrinth }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: bash tools/check-release.sh "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"
      - name: Read the CurseForge and Modrinth project ids
        id: projects
        run: |
          for site in curseforge modrinth; do
            id=$(awk -F= -v key="${site}_project_id" '$1 == key { print $2 }' gradle.properties)
            if [ -z "$id" ]; then
              echo "::notice::${site}_project_id is empty in gradle.properties, so this release skips ${site}."
            fi
            echo "${site}=${id}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          done

  checks:
    needs: verify
    uses: ./.github/workflows/checks.yml

  github:
    needs: checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1
        with:
          cache-provider: basic
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: jar
          path: dist
      - run: ./gradlew publishGithub -PpublishJar="dist/modular_planters-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.jar"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  curseforge:
    needs: [verify, github]
    if: needs.verify.outputs.curseforge != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1
        with:
          cache-provider: basic
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: jar
          path: dist
      - run: ./gradlew publishCurseforge -PpublishJar="dist/modular_planters-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.jar"
        env:
          CURSEFORGE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSEFORGE_API_KEY }}

  modrinth:
    needs: [verify, github]
    if: needs.verify.outputs.modrinth != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: microsoft
          java-version: "25"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1
        with:
          cache-provider: basic
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: jar
          path: dist
      - run: ./gradlew publishModrinth -PpublishJar="dist/modular_planters-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.jar"
        env:
          MODRINTH_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MODRINTH_API_KEY }}

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/sweetjp/.claude/skills/neoforge-mod-workflow

# NeoForge mod workflow

These rules sit on top of the `minecraft-modding` skill. That skill has the code patterns; this one decides versions, lookups, pacing and verification. Where they disagree, this one wins.

## Scope

- NeoForge only. If a request needs Fabric, Forge or a multiloader setup, say so and stop.
- Supported Minecraft versions:

| Version | Java | Mappings | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26.1 (default for new mods) | 25 | None. 26.x is unobfuscated and uses official names. | Start from the current NeoForge generator or MDK for that exact version. |
| 26.3 | 25 | None. | Same as 26.1. Check the NeoForge changelog for API changes since 26.1. |
| 1.21.1 | 21 | Mojang mappings plus Parchment. | NeoForge 21.1.x. Classes use `ResourceLocation`, not `Identifier`. |

- In an existing repo, the version is whatever `gradle.properties` says. Never change it, or any dependency version, unless asked.

## Looking things up

Never write an API name, method signature, registry name, event name or version number from memory. Check it first, in this order:

1. The `minecraft-modding` MCP server (adhi-jp), against the project's exact Minecraft version: `check-symbol-exists` or `batch-symbol-exists` before using a class or method, `get-class-source` and `get-class-members` to read vanilla code, `get-registry-data` for registry ids, `validate-access-transformer` after editing an access transformer, and `analyze-mod-jar` or `search-mod-source` for a dependency's API.
2. The NeoForge docs at `https://docs.neoforged.net` with the matching version selected, and the NeoForge changelog for that version.
3. Local clones under `~/DEV/git_repos` (see the `referencing-local-repos` skill), especially for addon APIs such as AE2.
4. The `minecraft-modding` skill's examples. Its `references/neoforge-api.md` is for 1.21.x only; for 26.x, use the sections labelled 26.x in `references/common-patterns.md`.

If a lookup fails and the answer still matters, say what could not be verified instead of guessing.

## Checkpoints

Work in small slices and stop at each checkpoint. Do not chain slices together without approval.

1. **Orient.** Read `gradle.properties`, the build script, `neoforge.mods.toml`, and the repo's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `justfile` if present. Follow the repo's own conventions over this skill's.
2. **Plan, then stop.** Before writing code, give a short plan: what changes, which files, which existing classes are reused, how it will be verified, and any open question. Wait for approval.
3. **Implement one slice.** One feature or one coherent part of a feature, never the whole backlog.
4. **Verify the slice** (see below), then **stop and report**: what changed, what was verified and how, and what was not verified. Propose the next slice instead of starting it.

Always ask before:

- adding, removing or upgrading a dependency, or editing `build.gradle`, `settings.gradle` or `gradle.properties`;
- deleting or renaming files, registry ids or config keys, because renames break existing worlds and configs;
- changing saved-data, attachment or data-component formats that existing worlds already contain;
- running `runClient` or `runServer`, which open long-running processes;
- anything the plan did not cover.

## Verification

Use the repo's `justfile` recipes when they exist; otherwise call Gradle directly.

| After | Run |
|---|---|
| Any Java change | `./gradlew build` (compiles and runs unit tests) |
| Gameplay logic: blocks, machines, recipes, entities, persistence | `./gradlew runGameTestServer`, plus each variant the repo's CI runs (for example optional-dependency flags) |
| Datagen providers changed | The repo's datagen task (`runData` or `runClientData`), then inspect the diff in the generated resources |
| Access transformer changed | `validate-access-transformer` through the MCP server, then a build |

Report failures with the actual error output. A slice that adds gameplay logic without a GameTest needs a stated reason.

Rules that apply to every slice:

- Server-authoritative logic. Validate every client packet.
- Client-only classes live in client packages and never load on a dedicated server.
- Every registered block or item gets its model, texture, language entry, loot table or recipe in the same slice. No missing textures or raw translation keys.
- Item state uses data components; world and entity state uses saved data or data attachments.

## Starting a new mod

For a new mod from an empty folder, copy `references/new-mod-prompt.md` (next to this file) into the new folder as `PROMPT.md`. Fill in its placeholders with the user rather than inventing them. The checkpoints above still apply: the design bible is the first checkpoint, then each MVP slice.

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Word each question so "yes" accepts your recommended answer.

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

## Env
- Maintain `~/.config/papercuts.md`, a global log shared by all my Claude sessions of anything that slowed down development. When you lose time to one mid-session, append date, symptom, fix, project. Check this file first when tooling fails mysteriously.
- obsidian vault at `~/obsidian/`
- macOS, Homebrew. Interactive shell is fish; zsh + zimfw is still installed. The Bash tool runs bash 5.3 (`CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL`), so tool commands use bash syntax and see no fish aliases or functions.
- Don't commit or push unless I say.
- `rg` skips hidden files and `.gitignore`d paths by default, so "no matches" is often a false negative. Use `--hidden` for dotfiles/`.gitlab/`/`.github/`, `--no-ignore` for ignored paths like `*.tfvars`, or `-uu` for both. (The PreToolUse hook `~/.claude/hooks/enforce-tools.sh` blocks bare `grep`, and `sed` substitutions in favor of `sd` or the Edit tool.)
- `fd` over `find`.
- In zsh, `noclobber` is on: `>` fails with "file exists" on an existing file and the stale content stays, so the next step silently reads old data. Use `>|` or `rm -f` first.
- zsh ties `path`/`status`/`argv` to shell internals; assigning to them wipes state (e.g. `$PATH`) and later commands die with "command not found". Use `ppath`, `pstate` instead.
- `bun`/`bunx` over `npm`/`npx` unless bun doesn't work for the project.

## Projects
- Personal code in `~/code`. Usually python + bash or fish.
- PEP 723 inline-metadata scripts (`uv run script.py`) over `uv run python3 <file>` when feasible; otherwise always `uv run python3`, never bare `python3`: scripts, modules, one-liners, REPL alike. (PreToolUse hook enforces this.)
- Scratch python: latest version.
- Scratch work: `~/tmp/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{short-description}`.
- Generalizable findings go to a runbook in `~/obsidian/AI Runbooks/`.
- `prek` (Rust), not `pre-commit`.
- Local shellscripts: fish syntax. Git repos: bash, falling back to POSIX unless bash-only syntax is certain to work.

## Corrections
- No unicode characters like emdashes `—`, ever.
- Hot reload is probably already running. Don't rebuild unless asked.
- Never mock sqlite. Real temp DB or nothing.
- Never add `Co-Authored-By: Claude` or other AI attribution trailers to commits, even if repo history has them.
- Don't add files when editing an existing one works.
- No hedging ("I think", "perhaps", "it might be worth"). No congratulating.
- Causal claims ("X caused Y"): say whether it's evidence or a guess.
- Unclear requirement -> ask. Don't fill in blanks.
- Repetition beats premature abstraction.
- Keep docs current on changes.
- A comment must pass all three tests or be deleted. Few comments, never compressed ones.
  1. Necessary: the code alone can't say it: why, cross-file links, intentional absences. Explaining how a common practice works (checksums, flags) always fails this.
  2. Skimmable: a full plain sentence that stands on its own. No jargon, no fragments.
  3. Complete: says what actually happens, end to end. Not just what doesn't happen, and not contradicted elsewhere in the file.

## Recall
At the start of non-trivial tasks and before architectural decisions, search past sessions for prior context. There is no skill named `recall`; the plugin logs each session to per-project files instead, and exposes `recall:show`, `recall:log` and `recall:save`.

- `<project>/.recall/context.md` is the condensed summary, `<project>/.recall/history.md` the full log. Read them directly.
- `.recall` is a dotfile, so a search needs `--hidden`: `rg --hidden "<term>" ~/.recall/history.md ~/DEV ~/code ~/tmp ~/.claude ~/prismlauncher ~/.ftba ~/.config ~/.local/minecraft --glob '**/.recall/*.md'` covers every project on this Mac in about a second. Logs from the old work machine are under `~/oldj_backups/ARC` and `~/oldj_backups/.claude/projects`.
- `recall:show` and `recall:log` only read the current project's files, and `recall:save` regenerates `context.md` from the log.

Read .entire/agent-guide.md for this repository's workflow, source inspection, and verification guidance.
@.entire/agent-guide.md

# Entire repository agent guide — Graph and Brain

Use Graph EVERY time you need to find code or a code relationship, not only at the
start. Both tools run, in this order, and neither replaces the other:

    1. entire brain brief "<task>" --json
    2. entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"

The brief answers why, and what was decided; the query answers where, and what
depends on it. Step 2 holds for small edits, follow-up work, and tasks that already
name the file: a named file answers where code is, not what else depends on it. Do
not skip either step on the grounds that the available context feels sufficient, and
do not treat having done one as having done the other.
Each later locate or relationship question MUST also go through Graph:

    entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"
    entire graph def --repo . --head --max-context-bytes 4096 <Name>
    entire graph neighbors --repo . --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --symbol <Name> --direction in
    entire graph impact --repo . --head --max-context-bytes 4096 --symbol <Name>

query finds the code for a description. def shows what a named symbol is.
neighbors lists callers (--direction in) or callees (--direction out). impact gives
the blast radius before you change a symbol. Use these, not grep, for definitions,
callers, references and dependents. Use grep/rg only for literal strings, config
keys, environment-variable names and file names.

--head reads the committed tree from a cache. Drop --head only when the answer
depends on uncommitted edits. The first call in a large repository can take tens of
seconds while that cache loads; later calls take about a second. Run the command
directly: it needs no timeout wrapper, and macOS has no timeout command.
A Coverage or Completeness line lists files Graph could not parse, often minified or
generated ones. It does not mean the results are partial; only a failure in the
language you asked about can hide a fact, and then you check that one relation in
source. Static relations can be incomplete: an empty result is not proof of no callers.

 - If the user asks about "ultrareview" or how to run it, explain that /code-review ultra launches a multi-agent cloud review of the current branch (or /code-review ultra <PR#> for a GitHub PR); /ultrareview is a deprecated alias for the same command. It is user-triggered and billed; you cannot launch it yourself, so do not attempt to via Bash or otherwise. It needs a git repository (offer to "git init" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/Users/sweetjp/.claude/projects/-Users-sweetjp-DEV-git-repos-minecraft-mods-ModularPlanters/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

Do build original games, games in a genre or with similar mechanics, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Don't build a recreation of a specific existing game (its name, characters, art, music, levels or look), even if it is renamed or called original.

Before you start, tell the user in a sentence or two what you plan to do. While you work, give the user a short update alongside your next tool call whenever you start a major new part of the work, change your plan, or launch something slow.

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.

WebSearch takes a `mode`. Use "standard" by default: it is the normal search, quick and cheap. Use "extended" only when a "standard" result comes back thin, off-target or possibly outdated, or from the start for hard-to-find or niche facts, very recent events, prices and availability, and multi-step research: it is thorough and fresh but several times the cost.
