[invariant] In ModularPlanters, any `MeLink` implementation (including the AE2 `MeBlockEntity` adapter) must return at most the requested amount from `insertItem`/extract calls: `OutputSink.insertInto`, `moveExportsInto` and `refillFrom` subtract the returned value without clamping, so over-reporting drives `remaining` negative and breaks the never-void-items rule.
[gotcha] AgriTech Evolved's in-game name for `agritechevolved:advanced_planter` is "Advanced Planter" and its MK3 speed item is "Speed Upgrade MK3". The ModularPlanters README and guide say "Powered Planter" and "MK3 Speed Modules", names that appear nowhere in ATE's lang file. [gotcha] The ModularPlanters repo is public and Entire's pre-push hook pushes session logs to `origin` along with code; the user must run `entire configure --skip-push-sessions` themselves to stop that (the agent should not run it).
[decision] Structure Lab is loaded into the ModularPlanters dev runClient only on the user's machine, via a `structureLabJar` path set in personal ~/.gradle/gradle.properties, so nothing Structure Lab-specific lands in the repo; the agent takes world screenshots through it, while GUI shots (Modular Planter Core screen, Modular Planter Block screen, Jade tooltip, guide page) are taken by the user.
[convention] Changes touching the Jade integration in Modular Planters are verified by running `./gradlew runGameTestServer` both normally and with `-PnoJade`, so the mod is confirmed to work without Jade installed.

=== rejected approaches and constraints for Modular Planters
[closed-negative] gradle/actions setup-gradle v6 was considered and rejected because upgrading to v6 accepts closed-source Terms of Use for its gradle-actions-caching component on the owner's behalf; pinned to v5.0.2 by SHA, revisit only if the owner explicitly accepts that licence.
[closed-negative] Slow seed trait upgrades in the planter were investigated and are not a planter bug. Productive Farming 0.13.0 rolls once per seed per harvest (3% at Mystical Agriculture tier 4, 2% at tier 5), raises one random trait, and does nothing if that trait is already maxed. The planter fires ATE's pre-harvest event per seed correctly. Revisit only if a seed's traits come back lower than what was inserted.
[decision] Modular Planters uses one running CHANGELOG.md with a `## <tag>` section per version, newest first, and the release workflow extracts only the matching section. The Oritech-style "next release only" file was rejected so every version's notes stay in the repo.
[invariant] ME transfers in Modular Planters must never void or duplicate items/energy; `MeLink` implementations clamp results with `Math.min(amount, ...)` and a simulated call must change nothing, because `moveExportsInto`/`refillFrom` arithmetic depends on that contract.
[decision] gradle/actions setup-gradle is on v6.4.1 (SHA-pinned) with cache-provider: basic in every workflow. The owner chose basic because it is the MIT @actions/cache implementation and avoids the proprietary gradle-actions-caching component whose Terms of Use made v6 a rejected option before; do not drop cache-provider: basic without the owner accepting those terms.
[invariant] AE2 and Applied Flux are compile-time-only optional dependencies in Modular Planters. All AE2 code lives in the `ae2` package and runs only behind `ModList.get().isLoaded("ae2")`, and the mod must load and work with any combination of the optional mods missing. Builds are verified with default, `-PnoAppliedFlux` and `-PnoAe2` runs.
[invariant] The mod must load without AE2: every generated data file referencing modular_planters:me or ae2 ids (recipe, loot table, advancement) carries a mod_loaded ae2 condition, the pickaxe tag entry is optional, and AE2 classes are referenced only from the ae2 package; verify with runGameTestServer -PnoAe2 (and -PnoAppliedFlux).

[gotcha] AgriTech Evolved's in-game name for `agritechevolved:advanced_planter` is "Advanced Planter" and its MK3 speed item is "Speed Upgrade MK3". The ModularPlanters README and guide say "Powered Planter" and "MK3 Speed Modules", names that appear nowhere in ATE's lang file. Renaming is an owner decision and must change README, spec and guide pages together.

1	# Modular Planters: brainstorm notes
2	
3	Status as of 2026-10-31: plans 1, 2 and 3 are built and on `main` at 83bfeac, pushed to `origin`; the `plan-1-working-multiblock` branch is deleted. Plan 4 (project pages, logo, contributor docs) is in brainstorm, with its design drafted and not yet approved; see "Next steps" item 12. The last runs passed `./gradlew test` and 126 GameTests with AE2, Applied Flux and Jade (124 without Applied Flux, 116 without AE2, 126 without Jade), and `./gradlew build` made the jar. The build targets NeoForge 26.1.2.116, the version ATM11 runs, and compiles against Jade 26.1.12 from Modrinth. The GitHub remote `origin` is `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`, which is public; main was first pushed on 2026-10-31. The Entire CLI is enabled in this repo, and its pre-push hook pushes session logs to `origin` along with any push.
4	
5	This session's Recall log and summary are in `.recall/` in this directory, copied from the shared log at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/.recall/history.md`.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	The farm runs about 390 to 400 Agritech: Evolved (ATE) Powered Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds:
10	
11	- 333 nickel planters feed the Lattice Reactor fuel line. Each has 2 MK3 speed modules, insanium farmland and a cloche, with no fertilizer. Source: `~/obsidian/Personal/Minecraft/Lattice Reactor Fuel Line.md`.
12	- Another 50 to 70 planters grow iron, diamond, coal and the other crafting resources.
13	
14	Each planter has its own Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Every planter you add means one more seed, soil, two modules and a pasted node.
15	
16	The mod is an ATE addon that collapses this into a few multiblocks. It's a consolidation, not a buff: a planter block holding 64 seeds should produce what 64 separate planters do, draw the same power and cost about the same to fully upgrade. The one deliberate buff is the built-in cloche's yield (see below).
17	
18	## Decisions
19	
20	All of these were agreed in the 2026-10-28 sessions.
21	
22	### Scope
23	
24	- The mod is called Modular Planters. You checked CurseForge and found no clashing names.
25	  - Mod id `modular_planters`, Java package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
26	  - GitHub repo `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`, cloned at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters` next to your Hostile-Neural-Networks fork. That location is my call: your CLAUDE.md says personal code goes in `~/code`, but that folder doesn't exist.
27	- A public mod for other players, with its source code on GitHub.
28	- MIT license, like ATE. All of the code is written for this mod. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0, so it's used only to see how a multiblock core links its parts and how its ME block talks to AE2. None of its code is copied in.
29	- NeoForge only, Minecraft 26.1.2.
30	- Hard dependency on ATE. Optional dependencies on Applied Energistics 2 (AE2), Applied Flux and Logistics Networks.
31	- In game, the mod reads ATE's live config, the same way a Powered Planter does. When a modpack changes ATE's numbers, a planter block still matches that pack's own Powered Planters. ATE's default config is used only for the planning math in these notes and for the tests. Settled on 2026-10-28 in the second session, from what was open question 6.
32	- Tests that verify the logic, plus manual play in the FTB Evolution 2 instance.
33	- Guide written for Oracle Index, the way Oritech does it.
34	
35	### Block lineup
36	
37	| Block | Job |
38	|---|---|
39	| Core | Forms the multiblock and owns the built-in cloche. Stores nothing itself. |
40	| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy lives, so the multiblock can't run without one. |
41	| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer and accepts it from pipes, LN or AE2. Shared by every planter block. |
42	| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |
43	| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. |
44	| ME (optional, needs AE2) | Joins an AE2 network. Sends outputs into ME storage and keeps the fertilizer block stocked. |
45	| Frame | Does nothing except link parts together. |
46	
47	There's no separate import block. The fertilizer block took its only job.
48	
49	The core is a doorway: energy sent into it goes to the power blocks, fertilizer goes to the fertilizer blocks, and outputs come out of the export blocks. That's what lets one LN node on the core run a whole multiblock with your current three-channel settings, as long as the node has an upgrade big enough for the multiblock (see Integrations). Each block also accepts its own resource directly, so cables and pipes can connect to the power, fertilizer or export blocks instead.
50	
51	### Planter block
52	
53	- Holds one seed type up to 64, soil or crux up to 64, and two module slots that hold up to 64 each. You fill all of these by hand in the planter block's screen.
54	- **Seed traits:** every seed keeps its own Productive Farming traits, so seeds of one type with different traits can go in together and each one levels on its own, the same as 64 Powered Planters (you chose this, option a). ATE's harvest events fire once per seed, each with that seed's own drops. Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum: Growth 3, Yield 3, Resistance 4 and Mutability 4 (`TraitsHelper.TRAIT_VALUES`).
55	- The number of seeds that actually grow is the smaller of seeds and soil. 64 seeds on 13 insanium farmland grow 13, and the screen says so.
56	- Accepts anything an ATE Powered Planter accepts, saplings included. It reads ATE's own planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`), so new ATE crops and KubeJS-added recipes work without changes.
57	- **Fertilizer:** each growing seed uses it at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so 64 seeds use what 64 planters would. If the fertilizer block is empty, or there isn't one, the planter blocks run unfertilized.
58	- **Power:** each seed draws what one Powered Planter with the same modules draws. If the multiblock can't cover a planter block's full draw for a tick, that block pauses. It doesn't run part of its seeds.
59	- **Outputs** go into the export blocks. When they're full, planter blocks pause until there's room. Nothing is voided.
60	
61	### Core screen
62	
63	- The core's screen lists every planter block in the multiblock and opens any of them, like the Logistics Networks Computer's Node Table lists nodes and opens their settings remotely. Planter blocks you can't reach in a build can still be restocked from the core.
64	- The layout in `mockups/core-screen.html` was approved in the second 2026-10-28 session:
65	  - The top of the screen shows the multiblock's totals: formed state and part count, stored power and draw, fertilizer, export fill, and ME status.
66	  - Rows are grouped by seed type under collapsible headings, the way LN groups nodes by label.
67	  - Each row shows the seed, how many seeds are growing, module coverage, a status (growing, short on soil, paused for power or for a full export, idle), and the block's position.
68	  - Each row has an outline button that highlights that planter block in the world, like LN's lamp, and an open button that brings up its screen.
69	  - A planter block's screen opened from the core is the same screen you get in the world, with a "Back to core" button added.
70	
71	### Textures
72	
73	- The blocks' textures are adapted from ATE's own, so they look like part of ATE. ATE is MIT, so ATE's copyright notice ships with the mod.
74	
75	### Upgrades
76	
77	These use ATE's own Speed and Yield Modules, MK1 to MK3. There are no new upgrade items.
78	
79	- Two module slots per planter block, like a Powered Planter. Each slot holds one module type, up to 64, so speed and yield can still be paired.
80	- Each module covers one seed. With 64 seeds and 23 MK3 speed modules, 23 seeds grow like upgraded planters and 41 like plain ones, and each group draws the power ATE would charge it.
81	- The slot shows how many modules are working: "23/64 seeds upgraded" when modules run short, or "13 working, 51 idle" when seeds run short.
82	- Why this option: the cost grows with the seeds, there's nothing new to balance, and if ATE retunes its modules the planter block follows automatically. A fixed-price bulk upgrade would be too cheap at 64 seeds and too expensive at 13. Capping each slot at the seed count fails when seeds are removed.
83	
84	### Recipes and progression
85	
86	- A player builds their first Modular Planter in the mid to late game. By then they already farm diamonds, emeralds and netherite, so recipes can use those without being a burden.
87	- The planter block is crafted from 64 Powered Planters in two steps, since crafting recipes don't usually take stacks of one item:
88	  1. 8 Powered Planters around a block of iron make a frame block. The frame is the multiblock's wall block, like ModularBees' part blocks, so the in-between step is a block you can use and not a crafting-only item.
89	  2. 8 frame blocks around an ATE Infused Farmland make a planter block.
90	- A frame placed to fill a gap or bridge two parts costs 8 Powered Planters, the same as one used in crafting. Iron was chosen over diamond for the center so filler frames don't also cost 9 diamonds each.
91	- Using Powered Planters means a pack that makes them cost more makes planter blocks cost more too. It also means existing Powered Planters can be broken and crafted straight into planter blocks. Your 333 nickel planters would make 5 planter blocks, with 13 left over.
92	- The power, fertilizer, export and ME blocks have their own recipes. Unlike ModularBees' parts, they aren't crafted from frames, which would add 8 Powered Planters to each.
93	- Each of the other blocks is built around the ATE block that does the same job (see "Other ATE blocks" under Research):
94	
95	| Block | Key ingredient |
96	|---|---|
97	| Core | ATE Cloche Dome, since the core is where the built-in cloche lives |
98	| Power | ATE Capacitor Tier 3 |
99	| Fertilizer | ATE Fertilizer Spreader |
100	| Export | ATE Silo |
101	| ME | AE2 ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`). The recipe has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`, so it only exists when AE2 is installed. |
102	
103	- The mid to late game gate sits on the power block. Every multiblock needs one, and a Tier 3 Capacitor requires diamonds and emeralds.
104	- The other ingredients and the grid patterns around each key ingredient are my calls. They go in the design document for you to check.
105	
106	### Built-in cloche
107	
108	- Always on. It uses ATE's configured cloche speed bonus, 1.15 by default.
109	- Yield change: ATE multiplies each drop count by the yield bonus and rounds to the nearest whole number, so a 1-item drop at 1.1 rounds back to 1 and the cloche's yield does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction instead: its configured yield bonus builds up a remainder on each harvest. With the default 1.1, a single-item drop gets one extra every tenth harvest. That's a 10% gain, never more than one extra item at a time.
110	
111	### Structure
112	
113	The structure is free form:
114	
115	- The multiblock is the core plus every part touching it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact doesn't count.
116	- Cap of 24 parts, not counting the core. Above that it doesn't form, and the core says why.
117	- It needs at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
118	- The core re-checks the shape when a part is placed or broken. If the shape breaks, the planter blocks stop but keep their contents.
119	
120	The guide shows three of the layouts from the session as example builds (see `mockups/layouts.html`):
121	
122	- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed layer, and a 3x3 glass canopy. The bed center and canopy center can't be clicked, so they take frame or glass.
123	- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor, floors of planter blocks above it and a glass roof.
124	- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the IO blocks take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks grow outward as four arms.
125	
126	### Integrations
127	
128	- **Logistics Networks: no dedicated block.** The block first proposed would mostly have been a rebuilt LN node. One node on the core does the same job, keeps your copy and paste workflow, and puts no LN code in the mod.
129	  - The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node without upgrades moves only 2,000 RF/t and 0.8 items a second, while one full planter block of the nickel setup draws 32,768 RF/t and puts out about 22 items a second.
130	  - A node uses the best upgrade in any of its slots for every channel. So one diamond upgrade covers up to 250,000 RF/t and 5,120 items a second, which is enough for 7 full planter blocks of the nickel setup. Above 7, the node needs a netherite upgrade.
131	  - The alternative to a netherite upgrade is more nodes, since each power block also accepts energy directly.
132	  - The guide needs to tell players this, with the numbers for each upgrade.
133	- **AE2: one ME block.** It sends outputs into ME storage the moment they're harvested, and keeps the fertilizer block stocked with a fertilizer you choose from ME. A block beats buses because the fuel line note flags import buses slowing to one pull every 40 ticks, and nickel alone makes about 5,300 essence a minute plus seeds and fertilized essence.
134	- **Applied Flux: optional, used by the ME block.** Plain AE2 doesn't carry FE, but Applied Flux lets an ME network store and deliver it. Applied Flux is installed in FTB Evolution 2, but not in ATM11. When both AE2 and Applied Flux are installed, the ME block also keeps the power blocks charged from the network's FE, so one ME connection runs power, fertilizer and outputs. Without Applied Flux the ME block handles only items and fertilizer, and power comes in through the core or the power blocks as usual. A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works, with no code in this mod.
135	
136	## Defaults I picked
137	
138	These are my calls, not things you decided. Change any of them.
139	
140	- The cloche's yield remainder applies to every drop the way ATE's yield bonus does, so seeds and fertilized essence get it too. It's kept per planter block and per item, and saved with the block so a reload doesn't lose it.
141	- The cap of 24 doesn't count the core.
142	- Several power blocks pool their storage. Several fertilizer blocks pool their fertilizer. Several export blocks fill one after another.
143	- A second ME block is refused, since it would do nothing.
144	- Frame blocks count toward the cap.
145	- If a part would join two cores, neither one forms. The core's screen names the problem block and its position, the way ModularBees does.
146	- When power runs short, a whole planter block pauses rather than part of it.
147	- With Applied Flux, the ME block draws from the network only enough FE to top the power blocks back up each tick. It doesn't fill them ahead of time.
148	- The core and power blocks accept energy at least as fast as the whole multiblock can draw it. They don't copy the low per-tick limit of ATE's capacitors, 8,192 RF/t at Tier 3, which would choke even one full planter block.
149	- Seeds in a planter block stay in the order you put them in, and the first ones grow when soil runs short. Hovering over the seed slot lists how many seeds have each trait combination.

# Modular Planters: brainstorm notes

Status as of 2026-10-31: plans 1, 2 and 3 are built and on `main` at 83bfeac, pushed to `origin`; the `plan-1-working-multiblock` branch is deleted. Plan 4 (project pages, logo, contributor docs) is in brainstorm, with its design drafted and not yet approved; see "Next steps" item 12. The last runs passed `./gradlew test` and 126 GameTests with AE2, Applied Flux and Jade (124 without Applied Flux, 116 without AE2, 126 without Jade), and `./gradlew build` made the jar. The build targets NeoForge 26.1.2.116, the version ATM11 runs, and compiles against Jade 26.1.12 from Modrinth. The GitHub remote `origin` is `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`, which is public; main was first pushed on 2026-10-31. The Entire CLI is enabled in this repo, and its pre-push hook pushes session logs to `origin` along with any push.

This session's Recall log and summary are in `.recall/` in this directory, copied from the shared log at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/.recall/history.md`.

## Why

The farm runs about 390 to 400 Agritech: Evolved (ATE) Powered Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds:

- 333 nickel planters feed the Lattice Reactor fuel line. Each has 2 MK3 speed modules, insanium farmland and a cloche, with no fertilizer. Source: `~/obsidian/Personal/Minecraft/Lattice Reactor Fuel Line.md`.
- Another 50 to 70 planters grow iron, diamond, coal and the other crafting resources.

Each planter has its own Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Every planter you add means one more seed, soil, two modules and a pasted node.

The mod is an ATE addon that collapses this into a few multiblocks. It's a consolidation, not a buff: a planter block holding 64 seeds should produce what 64 separate planters do, draw the same power and cost about the same to fully upgrade. The one deliberate buff is the built-in cloche's yield (see below).

## Decisions

All of these were agreed in the 2026-10-28 sessions.

### Scope

- The mod is called Modular Planters. You checked CurseForge and found no clashing names.
  - Mod id `modular_planters`, Java package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
  - GitHub repo `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`, cloned at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters` next to your Hostile-Neural-Networks fork. That location is my call: your CLAUDE.md says personal code goes in `~/code`, but that folder doesn't exist.
- A public mod for other players, with its source code on GitHub.
- MIT license, like ATE. All of the code is written for this mod. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0, so it's used only to see how a multiblock core links its parts and how its ME block talks to AE2. None of its code is copied in.
- NeoForge only, Minecraft 26.1.2.
- Hard dependency on ATE. Optional dependencies on Applied Energistics 2 (AE2), Applied Flux and Logistics Networks.
- In game, the mod reads ATE's live config, the same way a Powered Planter does. When a modpack changes ATE's numbers, a planter block still matches that pack's own Powered Planters. ATE's default config is used only for the planning math in these notes and for the tests. Settled on 2026-10-28 in the second session, from what was open question 6.
- Tests that verify the logic, plus manual play in the FTB Evolution 2 instance.
- Guide written for Oracle Index, the way Oritech does it.

### Block lineup

| Block | Job |
|---|---|
| Core | Forms the multiblock and owns the built-in cloche. Stores nothing itself. |
| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy lives, so the multiblock can't run without one. |
| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer and accepts it from pipes, LN or AE2. Shared by every planter block. |
| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |
| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. |
| ME (optional, needs AE2) | Joins an AE2 network. Sends outputs into ME storage and keeps the fertilizer block stocked. |
| Frame | Does nothing except link parts together. |

There's no separate import block. The fertilizer block took its only job.

The core is a doorway: energy sent into it goes to the power blocks, fertilizer goes to the fertilizer blocks, and outputs come out of the export blocks. That's what lets one LN node on the core run a whole multiblock with your current three-channel settings, as long as the node has an upgrade big enough for the multiblock (see Integrations). Each block also accepts its own resource directly, so cables and pipes can connect to the power, fertilizer or export blocks instead.

### Planter block

- Holds one seed type up to 64, soil or crux up to 64, and two module slots that hold up to 64 each. You fill all of these by hand in the planter block's screen.
- **Seed traits:** every seed keeps its own Productive Farming traits, so seeds of one type with different traits can go in together and each one levels on its own, the same as 64 Powered Planters (you chose this, option a). ATE's harvest events fire once per seed, each with that seed's own drops. Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum: Growth 3, Yield 3, Resistance 4 and Mutability 4 (`TraitsHelper.TRAIT_VALUES`).
- The number of seeds that actually grow is the smaller of seeds and soil. 64 seeds on 13 insanium farmland grow 13, and the screen says so.
- Accepts anything an ATE Powered Planter accepts, saplings included. It reads ATE's own planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`), so new ATE crops and KubeJS-added recipes work without changes.
- **Fertilizer:** each growing seed uses it at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so 64 seeds use what 64 planters would. If the fertilizer block is empty, or there isn't one, the planter blocks run unfertilized.
- **Power:** each seed draws what one Powered Planter with the same modules draws. If the multiblock can't cover a planter block's full draw for a tick, that block pauses. It doesn't run part of its seeds.
- **Outputs** go into the export blocks. When they're full, planter blocks pause until there's room. Nothing is voided.

### Core screen

- The core's screen lists every planter block in the multiblock and opens any of them, like the Logistics Networks Computer's Node Table lists nodes and opens their settings remotely. Planter blocks you can't reach in a build can still be restocked from the core.
- The layout in `mockups/core-screen.html` was approved in the second 2026-10-28 session:
  - The top of the screen shows the multiblock's totals: formed state and part count, stored power and draw, fertilizer, export fill, and ME status.
  - Rows are grouped by seed type under collapsible headings, the way LN groups nodes by label.
  - Each row shows the seed, how many seeds are growing, module coverage, a status (growing, short on soil, paused for power or for a full export, idle), and the block's position.
  - Each row has an outline button that highlights that planter block in the world, like LN's lamp, and an open button that brings up its screen.
  - A planter block's screen opened from the core is the same screen you get in the world, with a "Back to core" button added.

### Textures

- The blocks' textures are adapted from ATE's own, so they look like part of ATE. ATE is MIT, so ATE's copyright notice ships with the mod.

### Upgrades

These use ATE's own Speed and Yield Modules, MK1 to MK3. There are no new upgrade items.

- Two module slots per planter block, like a Powered Planter. Each slot holds one module type, up to 64, so speed and yield can still be paired.
- Each module covers one seed. With 64 seeds and 23 MK3 speed modules, 23 seeds grow like upgraded planters and 41 like plain ones, and each group draws the power ATE would charge it.
- The slot shows how many modules are working: "23/64 seeds upgraded" when modules run short, or "13 working, 51 idle" when seeds run short.
- Why this option: the cost grows with the seeds, there's nothing new to balance, and if ATE retunes its modules the planter block follows automatically. A fixed-price bulk upgrade would be too cheap at 64 seeds and too expensive at 13. Capping each slot at the seed count fails when seeds are removed.

### Recipes and progression

- A player builds their first Modular Planter in the mid to late game. By then they already farm diamonds, emeralds and netherite, so recipes can use those without being a burden.
- The planter block is crafted from 64 Powered Planters in two steps, since crafting recipes don't usually take stacks of one item:
  1. 8 Powered Planters around a block of iron make a frame block. The frame is the multiblock's wall block, like ModularBees' part blocks, so the in-between step is a block you can use and not a crafting-only item.
  2. 8 frame blocks around an ATE Infused Farmland make a planter block.
- A frame placed to fill a gap or bridge two parts costs 8 Powered Planters, the same as one used in crafting. Iron was chosen over diamond for the center so filler frames don't also cost 9 diamonds each.
- Using Powered Planters means a pack that makes them cost more makes planter blocks cost more too. It also means existing Powered Planters can be broken and crafted straight into planter blocks. Your 333 nickel planters would make 5 planter blocks, with 13 left over.
- The power, fertilizer, export and ME blocks have their own recipes. Unlike ModularBees' parts, they aren't crafted from frames, which would add 8 Powered Planters to each.
- Each of the other blocks is built around the ATE block that does the same job (see "Other ATE blocks" under Research):

| Block | Key ingredient |
|---|---|
| Core | ATE Cloche Dome, since the core is where the built-in cloche lives |
| Power | ATE Capacitor Tier 3 |
| Fertilizer | ATE Fertilizer Spreader |
| Export | ATE Silo |
| ME | AE2 ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`). The recipe has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`, so it only exists when AE2 is installed. |

- The mid to late game gate sits on the power block. Every multiblock needs one, and a Tier 3 Capacitor requires diamonds and emeralds.
- The other ingredients and the grid patterns around each key ingredient are my calls. They go in the design document for you to check.

### Built-in cloche

- Always on. It uses ATE's configured cloche speed bonus, 1.15 by default.
- Yield change: ATE multiplies each drop count by the yield bonus and rounds to the nearest whole number, so a 1-item drop at 1.1 rounds back to 1 and the cloche's yield does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction instead: its configured yield bonus builds up a remainder on each harvest. With the default 1.1, a single-item drop gets one extra every tenth harvest. That's a 10% gain, never more than one extra item at a time.

### Structure

The structure is free form:

- The multiblock is the core plus every part touching it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact doesn't count.
- Cap of 24 parts, not counting the core. Above that it doesn't form, and the core says why.
- It needs at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
- The core re-checks the shape when a part is placed or broken. If the shape breaks, the planter blocks stop but keep their contents.

The guide shows three of the layouts from the session as example builds (see `mockups/layouts.html`):

- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed layer, and a 3x3 glass canopy. The bed center and canopy center can't be clicked, so they take frame or glass.
- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor, floors of planter blocks above it and a glass roof.
- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the IO blocks take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks grow outward as four arms.

### Integrations

- **Logistics Networks: no dedicated block.** The block first proposed would mostly have been a rebuilt LN node. One node on the core does the same job, keeps your copy and paste workflow, and puts no LN code in the mod.
  - The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node without upgrades moves only 2,000 RF/t and 0.8 items a second, while one full planter block of the nickel setup draws 32,768 RF/t and puts out about 22 items a second.
  - A node uses the best upgrade in any of its slots for every channel. So one diamond upgrade covers up to 250,000 RF/t and 5,120 items a second, which is enough for 7 full planter blocks of the nickel setup. Above 7, the node needs a netherite upgrade.
  - The alternative to a netherite upgrade is more nodes, since each power block also accepts energy directly.
  - The guide needs to tell players this, with the numbers for each upgrade.
- **AE2: one ME block.** It sends outputs into ME storage the moment they're harvested, and keeps the fertilizer block stocked with a fertilizer you choose from ME. A block beats buses because the fuel line note flags import buses slowing to one pull every 40 ticks, and nickel alone makes about 5,300 essence a minute plus seeds and fertilized essence.
- **Applied Flux: optional, used by the ME block.** Plain AE2 doesn't carry FE, but Applied Flux lets an ME network store and deliver it. Applied Flux is installed in FTB Evolution 2, but not in ATM11. When both AE2 and Applied Flux are installed, the ME block also keeps the power blocks charged from the network's FE, so one ME connection runs power, fertilizer and outputs. Without Applied Flux the ME block handles only items and fertilizer, and power comes in through the core or the power blocks as usual. A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works, with no code in this mod.

## Defaults I picked

These are my calls, not things you decided. Change any of them.

- The cloche's yield remainder applies to every drop the way ATE's yield bonus does, so seeds and fertilized essence get it too. It's kept per planter block and per item, and saved with the block so a reload doesn't lose it.
- The cap of 24 doesn't count the core.
- Several power blocks pool their storage. Several fertilizer blocks pool their fertilizer. Several export blocks fill one after another.
- A second ME block is refused, since it would do nothing.
- Frame blocks count toward the cap.
- If a part would join two cores, neither one forms. The core's screen names the problem block and its position, the way ModularBees does.
- When power runs short, a whole planter block pauses rather than part of it.
- With Applied Flux, the ME block draws from the network only enough FE to top the power blocks back up each tick. It doesn't fill them ahead of time.
- The core and power blocks accept energy at least as fast as the whole multiblock can draw it. They don't copy the low per-tick limit of ATE's capacitors, 8,192 RF/t at Tier 3, which would choke even one full planter block.
- Seeds in a planter block stay in the order you put them in, and the first ones grow when soil runs short. Hovering over the seed slot lists how many seeds have each trait combination.
- If other mods add more drops than the outputs have room for, the extra is held in the planter block and it pauses until the extra is moved out. ATE's Powered Planter voids that extra instead.

## Still open

These are yours to decide:

- None left from the design. All of the earlier questions were settled in the second 2026-10-28 session.

### Local CI testing (parked 2026-11-05)

The Gradle 9.8.2 and setup-gradle v6.4.1 upgrade added `just ci` (runs the Build workflow in Docker with local-ci) and `just ci-lint` (actrun and zizmor). Both work, but neither ends green yet:

1. **`just ci-lint` always fails.** zizmor exits 14 on findings that were in the workflows before the upgrade: 19 `unpinned-uses` (the `actions/*@vN` tags), 3 `cache-poisoning` on `setup-gradle` in the release jobs, 8 `artipacked` (`actions/checkout` keeps credentials) and 2 `self-repository` (`./.github/workflows/checks.yml` could be `$/...`). Options: fix the findings, or have the recipe report them without failing. `actrun lint` only warns that the `verify` job's outputs are unused, which is wrong: `if: needs.verify.outputs...` uses them.
2. **`just ci` always shows 2 failed jobs out of 6.**
   - `generated-data`: local-ci checks files out with mode `rwxrwxrwx`, so `git status` lists all 46 generated files as changed with no content change. Changing the check to `git -c core.fileMode=false status --porcelain src/generated` fixes it locally and behaves the same on GitHub.
   - `prek`: local-ci replaces `git fetch` in the container, so `j178/prek-action` cannot clone the hook repos. No fix in this repo; run `just lint` instead.
3. **The Basic cache restore is unconfirmed.** Under local-ci the cache saves (with `cache-read-only: false`) but the next run does not find it. Check on GitHub: the second push to `main` after the upgrade should show "Entries: 1 restored" in the setup-gradle job summary.

The local-ci traps are also in `~/obsidian/AI Runbooks/Running GitHub Actions workflows locally.md`.

The items I said I'd settle myself (the power buffer, fertilizer and export slots, ME timing, Jade, JEI and the test setup) are settled in the design document, marked "(my call)".

## Research

### Agritech: Evolved

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/AgritechEvolved`. It's version 2.2.0.6, NeoForge 26.1.2.116 in `gradle.properties`, MIT license.

- Powered Planter code: `src/main/java/com/misterd/agritechevolved/blockentity/custom/AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity.java`.
- Slots: plant 0, soil 1, module 2 and 3, fertilizer 4, output 5 to 16. The plant, soil and module slots hold 1 item each (`getCapacityAsLong`).
- Growth time: `round(advanced_base_processing_time / (soil x modules x fertilizer x cloche))`, at line 435. `PlanterProcessingTimeEvent` can change it.
- Power per tick while growing: `round(base_power_consumption x module power multipliers)`, at line 318. No power means no progress that tick.
- Yield: `max(1, round(count x fertilizer x modules x cloche))` per drop, in `applyYieldModifier`, at line 674. That rounding is why a 1.1 cloche bonus disappears on single drops.
- Fertilizer: one item is consumed per harvest (`consumeFertilizer`). Its speed and yield multipliers come from the `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map (`FertilizerData`).
- Soil speed comes from the `agritechevolved:soil_modifiers` data map (`SoilModifierData`). Mystical Agradditions cruxes are soils in that map.
- Cloche: a block state property `CLOCHED` on the planter, applied with `ClocheItem`.
- Harvest events: `PlanterPreHarvestEvent` and `PlanterPostHarvestEvent`, which other mods may listen to.
- Version 2.2.0.6 fixed planters stalling when the output is full (issue #10). `hasOutputSpace` simulates the drop before harvesting.
- Example recipe: `src/main/resources/data/agritechevolved/recipe/planter/crop/mysticalagriculture/nickel_seeds.json` drops 1 essence (100%), 1 seed (20%) and 1 fertilized essence (10%).

ATE's settings are in `Config.java`, a common config with public static getters such as `Config.getPlanterBasePowerConsumption()` and `Config.getSpeedModuleMk3Multiplier()`. The Powered Planter reads its power, speed and buffer numbers through these getters, for example at lines 254, 318 and 331 of `AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity.java`. The addon can call the same getters to follow a pack's changes.

Default config values:

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| Base power consumption | 128 RF/t |
| Advanced planter base processing time | 600 ticks |
| Planter energy buffer | 100,000 RF |
| Speed MK1 / MK2 / MK3 | 1.5 / 1.75 / 2.0 speed, same as power multiplier |
| Yield MK1 / MK2 / MK3 | 1.5 / 1.75 / 2.0 yield, 0.95 / 0.90 / 0.75 speed penalty |
| Cloche | 1.15 speed, 1.10 yield |
| Insanium farmland | 1.75 growth |

Nickel per seed with defaults and 2 MK3 speed modules, insanium farmland and a cloche:

- Growth time is 600 / (1.75 x 2.0 x 2.0 x 1.15), about 74.5, rounded to 75 ticks. That's 16 harvests a minute.
- 16 essence a minute today. With the built-in cloche rule, 17.6 a minute.
- The reactor needs 5,313 essence a minute. That takes 333 seeds today, or about 302 with the built-in cloche.
- Power: 128 x 2.0 x 2.0 = 512 RF/t per seed. That's 32,768 RF/t for a full planter block, and about 170k RF/t for 333 seeds.

The fuel line note's numbers match these defaults.

#### Recipe costs

These come from ATE's default recipes in `src/generated/resources/data/agritechevolved/recipe/`. Modpacks can change them. Iron, gold, copper and netherite are counted in ingots, and blocks are converted at 9 ingots each.

| Item | Crafted from | Raw cost of one |
|---|---|---|
| Powered Planter (`advanced_planter`) | 1 basic planter, 3 iron blocks, 2 iron, 2 redstone | 1 basic planter, 29 iron, 2 redstone |
| Cloche (`cloche_dome`, makes 4) | 8 iron, 1 glass | 2 iron, a quarter of a glass block |

Each module tier is crafted from the tier below it, so the raw cost includes every earlier tier.

| Module | Crafted from | Raw cost of one | Raw cost of 64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speed MK1 (`sm_mk1`) | 2 iron, 1 gold, 2 redstone | 2 iron, 1 gold, 2 redstone | 128 iron, 64 gold, 128 redstone |
| Speed MK2 (`sm_mk2`) | Speed MK1, 2 gold blocks, 2 diamonds | 2 diamonds, 19 gold, 2 iron, 2 redstone | 128 diamonds, 1,216 gold, 128 iron, 128 redstone |
| Speed MK3 (`sm_mk3`) | Speed MK2, 4 emerald blocks, 2 diamond blocks, 2 netherite | 2 netherite, 20 diamonds, 36 emeralds, 19 gold, 2 iron, 2 redstone | 128 netherite, 1,280 diamonds, 2,304 emeralds, 1,216 gold, 128 iron, 128 redstone |
| Yield MK1 (`ym_mk1`) | 1 copper block, 2 wheat, 2 wheat seeds | 9 copper, 2 wheat, 2 wheat seeds | 576 copper, 128 wheat, 128 wheat seeds |
| Yield MK2 (`ym_mk2`) | Yield MK1, 2 gold blocks, 2 copper blocks | 27 copper, 18 gold, 2 wheat, 2 wheat seeds | 1,728 copper, 1,152 gold, 128 wheat, 128 wheat seeds |
| Yield MK3 (`ym_mk3`) | Yield MK2, 4 enchanted golden apples, 2 gold blocks, 2 netherite | 4 enchanted golden apples, 2 netherite, 27 copper, 36 gold, 2 wheat, 2 wheat seeds | 256 enchanted golden apples, 128 netherite, 1,728 copper, 2,304 gold, 128 wheat, 128 wheat seeds |

Other ATE blocks that do one of our blocks' jobs, with their default recipes and settings:

| ATE block | What it does | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| Capacitor Tier 1 (`capacitor_tier1`) | Stores and distributes RF. 500,000 RF, 512 RF/t. | 1 copper block, 2 iron, 6 redstone |
| Capacitor Tier 2 (`capacitor_tier2`) | 1,000,000 RF, 2,048 RF/t. | Tier 1, 6 redstone blocks, 2 gold |
| Capacitor Tier 3 (`capacitor_tier3`) | 4,000,000 RF, 8,192 RF/t. | Tier 2, 6 diamonds, 2 emeralds |
| Silo (`silo`) | Pulls outputs out of planters within range into 63 slots. Takes a range module. | 7 iron, 1 chest, 1 observer |
| Fertilizer Spreader (`fertilizer_spreader`) | Pushes fertilizer from 63 slots into planters within range. Takes a range module. | 7 iron, 1 chest, 1 dispenser |
| Infused Farmland (`infused_farmland`) | ATE's own soil, 1.5 growth speed in a planter. | Mulch and a hoe, shapeless. Mulch is 8 compacted biomass around farmland, making 2. |

ATE's block textures are in `src/main/resources/assets/agritechevolved/textures/block/`, among them `capacitor_*`, `dome_*` and the planter textures. The repo's `LICENSE.txt` is MIT, and the README sets no separate terms for textures. So they can be edited and reused, as long as ATE's copyright notice ships with the mod.

The capacitor numbers are from `Config.java`. The silo and spreader behavior is from `SiloBlockEntity.java` and `FertilizerSpreaderBlockEntity.java`.

Vanilla 26.1.2 has no crafting recipe for enchanted golden apples, so they only come from loot. The 26.1.2 client jar has `data/minecraft/recipe/golden_apple.json` but no enchanted version. Unless a pack adds a recipe, Yield MK3 is limited by loot, at 4 apples per module.

For 64 seeds with 2 MK3 speed modules each, as in the nickel setup:

- 64 Powered Planters and 64 cloches: about 1,980 iron, 128 redstone, 64 basic planters and 16 glass.
- 128 MK3 speed modules, twice the "64" column: 256 netherite, 2,560 diamonds, 4,608 emeralds, 2,432 gold, 256 iron and 256 redstone.

The modules are nearly all of the cost, and the planter block already charges for them one per seed.

### ModularBees

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularBees`. It's NeoForge 26.1.2.59-beta, LGPL-3.0 license, package `com.glodblock.github.modularbees`.

- Multiblock base: `common/tileentities/base/TileMBModularCore.java`. It holds a `refresh` flag, `formStructure()`, `buildStructure()` returning a `TryResult` with a message and position, and `logicTick()` that only runs while formed. Parts extend `TileMBModularComponent` and link to one core. `util/StructureListener` watches for block changes.
- The centrifuge shape is in `TileModularCentrifuge.getPoses()`: 3x3 layers at core y-1 (corners only), y and y+1. Any centrifuge part fits any slot, with at most one heater. The beehive is a fixed 3x3x3.
- The import block (`TileCentrifugeImport`) pulls from the container it faces every `AUTO_IMPORT_INTERVAL`.
- Recipes are in `datagen/MBRecipeProvider.java`. The plain beehive part block (`modular_beehive_part`) is cheap: 8 scented planks around iron bars. Every other beehive part, such as the export, feeder, treater and overclocker, has a part block as one of its ingredients.
- The ME export block's recipe (`me_beehive_export.json`) is an ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), 2 fluix crystals, 2 iron bars and a modular export block. It has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`, so it only exists when AE2 is installed.
- AE2 integration lives in `xmod/ae/`. `TileMEExport` extends `TileAENetworkHost`, inserts with `AEItemKey`, has a 12-slot filter with a whitelist toggle, and pushes every `ME_EXPORT_INTERVAL`. The core collects parts that implement `MEExportAction` and calls `sendToMENetwork`.

### Applied Flux

The installed jar is `AppliedFlux-26.1-1.0.2-neoforge.jar`, by GlodBlock, who also wrote ModularBees. Its package is `com.glodblock.github.appflux`.

- It comes as a block (`TileFluxAccessor`) and as a cable part (`PartFluxAccessor`). Both join the AE2 grid.
- It has an input/output mode, blocked sides, a fast mode, and an `EnergyDistributeService` that pushes FE into neighbors' energy storage (`distribute`).
- It's in FTB Evolution 2 but not ATM11, which has no Applied Flux and no Flux Networks.

### Logistics Networks

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/LogisticsNetworks`.

- A node sticks onto one block and has 9 channels. It moves items, fluids, FE and Mekanism chemicals, and works with any block that exposes those capabilities.
- Tags `logisticsnetwork:blacklist/block` and the item, fluid and chemical variants stop nodes or transfers. The mod must not end up in them.
- Upgrade limits are in `upgrade/UpgradeLimitsConfig.java` (`defaultForTier`), and a server can change them in its config. A node's tier is the best upgrade in any of its slots (`NodeUpgradeData.getUpgradeTier`). Energy channels run every tick no matter the tier (`TransferEngine.cooldownRemaining`). Item channels run once every "min ticks".

| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items per run | Min ticks between item runs | Items a second |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | 2,000 RF | 16 | 20 | 0.8 |
| Iron | 10,000 RF | 32 | 10 | 64 |
| Gold | 50,000 RF | 64 | 5 | 256 |
| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 256 | 1 | 5,120 |
| Netherite | 2,147,483,647 RF | 10,000 | 1 | 200,000 |

- One full planter block of the nickel setup harvests 1,024 times a minute. That's 1,024 essence, about 205 seeds and about 102 fertilized essence, so about 22 items a second, or about 24 with the built-in cloche.
- With your maxed nickel seeds, one full planter block puts out about 310 items a second, or about 319 with the built-in cloche (see "Productive Farming seed traits"). That's more than a gold upgrade's 256, so even one planter block needs a diamond upgrade. Diamond moves enough items for about 16 such planter blocks, but its 250,000 RF/t covers only 7.
- The Computer block's Node Table is the model for the core's screen. Its guide page is `src/main/resources/assets/logisticsnetworks/guides/logisticsnetworks/guide/computer/node-table.md`. Each row shows the block's icon and name, its dimension and coordinates, a lamp button that outlines the node in the world, and a gear button that opens the node's screen remotely. Labeled nodes are grouped under collapsible headers, and the remote screen has a "Back to table" button.

### Productive Farming seed traits

The design document's reviewer found this, and I checked it on 2026-10-28.

- Productive Farming 0.13.0 (`productivefarming-26.1.2-0.13.0.jar`) is installed in FTB Evolution 2. Its repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/productivefarming`, branch `origin/dev-26.1`.
- `integrations/agritech/AgriTechEvolvedEventHandler.java` listens to all three ATE planter events:
  - **`PlanterProcessingTimeEvent`:** divides growth time by (Growth level + 1).
  - **`PlanterPreHarvestEvent`:** each harvest may raise one random trait on the planted seed. ATE writes the changed seed back into the seed slot (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584).
  - **`PlanterPostHarvestEvent`:** adds the Yield level to every drop stack that isn't a seed, and copies the traits onto dropped seeds (`AgriTechStatsHelper.applyStats`). It adds to each stack, not each item, so the event has to see one stack per seed for 64 seeds to get 64 times the bonus.
- The traits are Growth and Yield (0 to 3), and Resistance and Mutability (0 to 4). Seeds whose traits differ don't stack.
- The pack's `config/productivefarming-server.toml` sets `statsOnExternalCrops = true`, and PF's `external_seeds` tag includes `#mysticalagriculture:seeds`. So Mystical Agriculture seeds in ATE planters gain traits.
- Nickel is in `productivefarming:mystical_tier_4`, and `data_maps/item/stat_increase_chance.json` gives that tier 0.03. That's a 3% chance per harvest to raise one trait.
- Maxed Growth 3 and Yield 3 make a planter 4 times as fast with 4 essence per harvest, so about 16 times the essence.
- **Decision:** every seed keeps its own traits (option a). The design document's "Seed traits" section has the details.

Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum. These numbers are calculated from the code and that statement, not measured in game:

- **Growth:** the 75-tick harvest becomes `max(1, round(75 / 4))` = 19 ticks, about 63.2 harvests a minute instead of 16.
- **Essence:** 1 + 3 = 4 per harvest, so about 252.6 essence a minute per planter. The built-in cloche adds 0.1 a harvest, about 258.9.
- **Other drops:** fertilized essence gets the Yield bonus too, 0.4 a harvest. Seeds don't, 0.2 a harvest.
- **Power:** unchanged at 512 RF/t a planter, since traits don't change power per tick.
- **The reactor:** the fuel line needs 5,313 nickel essence a minute. The fuel line note sized 333 planters at 16 essence a minute each, with no traits. At about 252.6 each, 22 maxed planters cover it, or 21 with the built-in cloche.
- **What 333 maxed planters make:** about 84,000 essence a minute, about 16 times what the reactor burns. If the farm in game makes about 5,300 a minute instead, one of these readings is wrong, and the design's per-seed events depend on it.

### Oracle Index, as Oritech uses it

The Oracle Index repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index`, and Oritech's is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech`.

- Pages use the moddedmc.wiki layout: a `wiki/` folder with `sinytra-wiki.json` (id, platforms, owners), `docs/` and `content/` folders, `_meta.json` files for ordering, and `.mdx` pages with front matter (`id`, `type`, `title`).
- Oritech copies `wiki/` into `assets/oracle_index/books/oritech` in `processResources`, leaving out `assets/item/**`. Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it's optional at runtime.
- Oritech uses the `org.moddedmc.wiki.toolkit` Gradle plugin, plus the wiki exporter (`wiki-exporter.json`, a `wikiExport` run config) to render item images.
- Supported page components: markdown, crafting recipes, images (assets), callouts, audio and video embeds. There are no 3D or rotatable scenes like AE2's GameScenes, so the example builds will be still images.

The instance is at `~/.ftba/instances/ftb evolution 2`. It runs pack version 1.5.1 with NeoForge 26.1.2.121, ZGC and an 8 GB heap.

ModularBees is not in this instance.

# Contributing to Modular Planters

Contributions are welcome: bug fixes, compatibility fixes, guide corrections and code improvements.

I have a specific vision for the mod and what content fits it. Before working on new content or a balance change, please open an issue and talk it through first, so your time isn't spent on something that won't be merged.

## Issues

- Search the open and closed issues first. Your bug or idea may already be there.
- Use the bug report or feature request form. For bugs, a log link and steps to reproduce make the biggest difference.

## Pull requests

- Make one pull request per change. Separate fixes are easier to review and to revert.
- Link the issue the pull request fixes.
- Say how you tested it. At least run `just check` and `just lint`, and check client-side changes in game and on a dedicated server.
- Run `prek install` once in your clone, so each commit is formatted the way the Build workflow checks it.
- Check your spelling and grammar in text players see, such as the guide in `wiki/` and the lang entries.

[DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) explains how to set up the project and run it locally.

# Contributing to Modular Planters

Contributions are welcome: bug fixes, compatibility fixes, guide corrections and code improvements.

I have a specific vision for the mod and what content fits it. Before working on new content or a balance change, please open an issue and talk it through first, so your time isn't spent on something that won't be merged.

## Issues

- Search the open and closed issues first. Your bug or idea may already be there.
- Use the bug report or feature request form. For bugs, a log link and steps to reproduce make the biggest difference.

## Pull requests

- Make one pull request per change. Separate fixes are easier to review and to revert.
- Link the issue the pull request fixes.
- Say how you tested it. At least run `just check` and `just lint`, and check client-side changes in game and on a dedicated server.
- Run `prek install` once in your clone, so each commit is formatted the way the Build workflow checks it.
- Check your spelling and grammar in text players see, such as the guide in `wiki/` and the lang entries.

[DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) explains how to set up the project and run it locally.

| **Fabric** | 26.x current; 1.21.11 examples retained | Java 25 current; Java 21 on 1.21.x | Gradle + Fabric Loom |
| **Architectury** (multiloader) | 26.x or 1.21.x | Match Minecraft | Gradle + Architectury Loom |

Always confirm the platform and Minecraft version from `gradle.properties` or `build.gradle`
before writing any mod-specific code.

projects, start from the current loader generator or example mod and preserve
its build layout. Do not copy the 1.21.11 mapping, Loom plugin, remapping task,
or Java 21 snippets in this skill into a 26.x project. Fabric 26.x uses the
non-remapping Loom path and official names; NeoForge 26.x should start from the
current NeoForge generator. The detailed API references cover legacy 1.21.x
examples unless a section explicitly says 26.x.

=== commit message style branch merge workflow
[preference] The owner wants Java formatted per the Google Java style guide (google-java-format via prek) and Prettier for markdown, yaml and json, with JSON exempt from the final-newline rule; no mention of ARC may appear in any committed file or commit message.
[invariant] In ModularPlanters, the local `gradle.properties` change that downgrades `neo_version` for the ATM11 pack must never be committed, and the same applies to `.claude/settings.json.graphify-bak`. Both files stay in the working tree but out of every commit.
[decision] Modular Planters uses one running CHANGELOG.md with a `## <tag>` section per version, newest first, and the release workflow extracts only the matching section. The Oritech-style "next release only" file was rejected so every version's notes stay in the repo.
[preference] The user wants Java formatted to the Google Java Style Guide via google-java-format (2-space indents, 100 columns), with a tracked .editorconfig so IntelliJ matches, and Prettier for Markdown, YAML and JSON, with JSON exempt from the end-of-file-newline hook.
[decision] Player-facing Modular Planters docs use the in-game block names from en_us.json ("Modular Planter Core", "Modular Planter Block", "Modular Planter Frame", etc.), not shorthand names.
[gotcha] Java `assert` statements do nothing in GameTests because the GameTest server JVM does not run with -ea; use `if (!cond) { helper.fail(...); return; }` instead.
[convention] Changes touching the Jade integration in Modular Planters are verified by running `./gradlew runGameTestServer` both normally and with `-PnoJade`, so the mod is confirmed to work without Jade installed.
[preference] The user wants the JetBrains MCP servers (idea, pycharm, rider) and opentofu configured per repo through a `.mcp.json`, which the user confirms manually, not at user level. The context7 plugin was removed entirely.
[gotcha] Jade swallows plugin exceptions, so passing GameTests with Jade loaded does not prove MPJadePlugin registered or renders tooltips. Only a manual in-game check, recorded in NOTES.md, verifies the Jade tooltips and the Oracle Index book.
[preference] User takes Modular Planters screenshots in the dev runClient (faster than modpack instances); the agent takes world shots via the local Structure Lab mod, and the user takes only GUI shots (Core screen, Planter Block screen, Jade tooltip, guide page).
=== documentation rules player facing naming lang guide
[decision] Player-facing Modular Planters docs use the in-game block names from en_us.json ("Modular Planter Core", "Modular Planter Block", "Modular Planter Frame", etc.), not shorthand names.
[decision] Modular Planters README targets repo browsers/devs (logo, summary, screenshots, links, build-from-source, license); player reference (building rules, recipes, config, Logistics Networks numbers) moves to the in-game guide; CONTRIBUTING follows Oritech's rules (ask in an issue before content/balance changes).
[gotcha] AgriTech Evolved's in-game name for `agritechevolved:advanced_planter` is "Advanced Planter" and its MK3 speed item is "Speed Upgrade MK3". The ModularPlanters README and guide say "Powered Planter" and "MK3 Speed Modules", names that appear nowhere in ATE's lang file. Renaming is an owner decision and must change README, spec and guide pages together.
[convention] README.md is the source of truth for the Oracle Index guide in `wiki/` (docs/, content/, assets/). Guide pages copy README text rather than paraphrase it, and WikiStructureTest checks block pages against the generated recipe JSON.
[gotcha] In GameTest (MC 26.1), `makeMockPlayer(GameType.CREATIVE)` only overrides `gameMode()`, so `hasInfiniteMaterials()` stays false and vanilla CLONE clicks are no-ops; tests must also set `abilities.instabuild = true`.
[gotcha] Structure Lab freezes game ticks on world load and puts the player in spectator, so a Modular Planter Core never forms and crops never grow until `/tick unfreeze` (and `/gamemode creative` for normal play); it also deletes the previous capture set whenever a new structure is submitted, so copy shots out first.
[gotcha] Guide pages in `wiki/` are MDX, so angle-bracket placeholders like `<problem>` are parsed as JSX tags and break page rendering. Write them as plain words instead (for example "Not formed:" followed by the problem).
[gotcha] Java `assert` statements do nothing in GameTests because the GameTest server JVM does not run with -ea; use `if (!cond) { helper.fail(...); return; }` instead.
[preference] User takes Modular Planters screenshots in the dev runClient (faster than modpack instances); the agent takes world shots via the local Structure Lab mod, and the user takes only GUI shots (Core screen, Planter Block screen, Jade tooltip, guide page).
[preference] The owner wants Java formatted per the Google Java style guide (google-java-format via prek) and Prettier for markdown, yaml and json, with JSON exempt from the final-newline rule; no mention of ARC may appear in any committed file or commit message.
=== data format save key rename compatibility
[invariant] The Planter Block save key stays "soil_and_modules" despite the module-to-upgrade rename, so Planter Blocks in existing worlds keep their soil and upgrades; ATE's own names (ATETags.Items.ATE_MODULES, getSpeedModuleMk1Multiplier etc.) must also not be renamed.
[invariant] gradle.properties `neo_version` was deliberately lowered from 121 to 116 so the mod runs in the ATM11 modpack. Do not bump it back without checking pack compatibility. The user tests in ATM11 and FTB Evolution 2 instances under ~/prismlauncher/.
[preference] The owner wants Java formatted per the Google Java style guide (google-java-format via prek) and Prettier for markdown, yaml and json, with JSON exempt from the final-newline rule; no mention of ARC may appear in any committed file or commit message.
[preference] The user wants Java formatted to the Google Java Style Guide via google-java-format (2-space indents, 100 columns), with a tracked .editorconfig so IntelliJ matches, and Prettier for Markdown, YAML and JSON, with JSON exempt from the end-of-file-newline hook.
[gotcha] Jade (26.1.12) rejects a plugin whose data provider also implements IComponentProvider ("Data providers cannot implement IComponentProvider"), but only checks this on a physical client, so GameTest servers never catch it; Modular Planters therefore splits each block into a server-data provider and a separate tooltip provider (Oritech's pattern), and the JadeTests GameTest checks this with isAssignableFrom.
[decision] Modular Planters CurseForge/Modrinth page text lives in docs/description.md with images in docs/media/ (linked by GitHub URLs on main); .gitignore ignores only /docs/superpowers/ so specs/plans stay untracked while page files are tracked.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/sweetjp/.claude/skills/julian-voice

# Julian's Voice

Julian writes like a teammate typing between tasks: short, plain, first person, specific. Most messages are 1-3 sentences of 10-35 words. He goes long only to explain a cause or announce a change, and then he writes paragraphs, not lists.

## This skill overrides chat-style rules

Caveman mode, terse-output rules, and the "no hedging" rule in CLAUDE.md govern how Claude talks to Julian. They do not apply to drafts written as Julian. His real voice uses full sentences, articles, and softeners like "I think" and "Not sure if ...?". Keep them. If a humanizer pass runs afterwards, this skill wins on conflicts.

## Before drafting

Read the examples file for the context you are writing in. Match its length and shape before you match its words.

| Context | Examples file |
|---|---|
| Chat DM or channel | `examples/chat.md` |
| PR review comment or reply | `examples/pr-comments.md` |
| PR title, PR description, commit message | `examples/pr-and-commits.md` |
| GitHub issue or issue comment | `examples/issues.md` |

## After drafting

Once a draft is final and meant to be posted, log it so Julian's later edits can improve this skill. Pass the draft text on stdin:

```bash
uv run ~/.claude/skills/julian-voice/scripts/feedback.py draft --context <context> --target <target>
```

| Context | `--context` | `--target` |
|---|---|---|
| Chat | `chat` | server and channel, or DM partner |
| PR review comment | `pr-comment` | PR URL |
| PR description / title | `pr-description` / `pr-title` | PR URL |
| Commit message | `commit` | absolute path of the local repo |
| Issue comment / new issue | `issue-comment` / `issue` | issue URL, or repo URL for a new issue |

Log one entry per piece of text. A PR title and its description are two entries. When Julian asks to review voice feedback, follow `FEEDBACK.md` in this skill's directory.

## Shape by context

**Chat.** Median 19 words. Lowercase starts and no final period are normal. Casual words are normal: "y'all", "gonna", "cuz", "rq", "iirc", "lol". End with a `:shortcode:` emoji when one fits (`:+1:`, `:joy:`, `:shrug:`, `:facepalm:`). Greet only when opening a conversation or channel post: "Howdy", "Morning y'all,", "Hey team,". Links go on their own line with a one-line description. Times look like "1230 EST".

**PR review comment.** Median 16 words. Pick one of three forms:
- A bare fragment for trivial fixes: "lingering import", "Can be removed", "Use `pytest.approx` instead."
- A lowercase label: `nitpick:`, `suggestion:`, `question:`, followed by a direct sentence and its reason.
- A question for judgment calls: "Would it make sense to ...?", "Is there a way to ...?", "What do you think about ...?", followed by "Mostly asking since ...".

Put code after "something like this:" in an untagged fence. Identifiers go in backticks. Link docs as evidence.

**Replying to review.**
- Accepting: "Good catch, changed." / "Good point." / "Thanks for catching that." plus what you did.
- Your own mistake: "Whoops," / "Shoot," / "my bad" plus the fix in one clause.
- Changing your mind later: "Coming back to this, ..." or "The more I thought about it, ...".
- Pushing back: concede part first ("I agree, but ...", "True, and ..."), then the concrete reason. For a strong position use "I'm going to push against ... because ...".
- Approving: "LGTM, rebase your branch and then I'll approve :thumbsup:".

**PR title.** Check the repo's recent history with `git log` first. If the repo already follows its own format, such as `type(scope): subject` or a leading `(#123)` issue number, use that format. Otherwise the format is `type: subject`.
- **Types:** `feat`, `fix`, `ci`, `chore`, `doc`, `revert`, `test`. A breaking change is `feat!:`.
- **Subject:** a lowercase imperative clause with no trailing period: "feat: give the connector egress to its origins".
- **Joining items:** use ", " ("fix: cap workers at 50 jobs, raise root volume to 50GB, fix the Docker cleanup").
- **Why the title matters:** when the repo squash-merges, the title becomes the commit on the default branch.

The older styles (`KEY-N - Adding ...`, `NOREF - ...`) in `examples/pr-and-commits.md` are history. Use them only when Julian asks for that style.

**PR description.** Median 20 words. Open with the non-obvious fact, the reason, a link ("See <url>"), or "Also ...". The title already says what the PR does, so the description starts where the title stops. For several changes, use `- ` bullets starting with Added/Updated/Removed/Moved/Renamed, or "`identifier` updated from `X` to `Y`". Give each reason inline ("as", "since", "in favor of") or in a nested sub-bullet. Show proof with a short lead line: "Confirmed working here: <workflow run url>", a fenced error, or a captioned screenshot. End after the last fact. Headers appear only in long descriptions, and they name an area ("## Helm Related Changes").

**Commit message.** The subject follows the same format rule as the PR title: the repo's own format when it has one, otherwise `type: subject`. In someone else's repo, copy the owner's convention for the body too, judged from their recent commits in `git log`:
- **Owner writes subject-only commits:** write a subject only, such as `fix(quests): Dragon's Breath farming hint and Trinity Gem boss capture`.
- **Owner writes bodies:** wrap at 80 columns and walk the cause. Open with what is broken ("Without this patch applied, ..."), trace it through exact `Class#method` names, then say what "This patch ..." changes and what stays unaffected. `examples/pr-and-commits.md` has a full example.
- **Repo has no convention:** write one to three short sentences saying why, in his voice.

```
fix: publish releases with an image that has the gh cli

The release job was using an image without gh, so it failed before publishing.
```

**GitHub issue.** Start with "As an engineer, I want to ..." or a plain problem statement. Follow with evidence (error text, workflow run link). Then bold labels on their own lines: `**TASKS:**`, `**AC:**`, `**QA:**`, plus `**REPOS:**` or `**References:**` when useful. Tasks name exact variables, paths, and values. AC are observable outcomes. Small issues can be one or two lines.

**Issue comment.** Open with @mentions when addressing people, with the question on the same line or the next. Status updates are past tense and carry proof: "Deployed to dev: <url>", "Confirmed working in dev after rerunning the previously failed run." Close issues with "Marking as won't do, as ..." or "Implemented with <link>". Put any "cc @Name" line last. No "!" and no emoji.

## Habits across contexts

- **Requests:** "When you get a chance, do you mind ...?" plus why. "Please" is rare.
- **Hedges:** one per message, placed before the claim, followed by the reason. Use "I think", "Not sure if ...?", "I believe", "probably", "imo", or "(could be wrong on this)".
- **Questions:** state your own guess and end with "right?" or "correct?". Ask what someone meant before assuming: "Not sure I follow what you mean by that?"
- **Causes:** "The issue is that ...". Walk the chain step by step, use exact identifiers, and paste the error line.
- **Linkers:** "That way ...", "On top of that, ...", "instead of", "for some reason", "e.g.", "~" for approximate numbers ("~3-5 minutes").
- **Emphasis:** `_underscore_` italics or one word in CAPS ("MUCH", "NOT"). Bold appears only as issue section labels.
- **Humor:** dry, aimed at himself or at the tools, never at the reviewer.

## Swap these for his forms

| Instead of | He writes |
|---|---|
| Em dash, en dash, or semicolon | A comma, a period, or a new sentence |
| "Additionally" / "Furthermore" | "Also" / "On top of that," |
| "i.e." | "e.g." or "for example" |
| "Great question!" / "Thanks for the thorough review!" | Get straight to the answer |
| "Hope this helps" / "Let me know your thoughts!" | Stop after the last fact. Use "Let me know" only when tied to a specific action. |

Base directory for this skill: /Users/sweetjp/.claude/skills/julian-voice

# Julian's Voice

Julian writes like a teammate typing between tasks: short, plain, first person, specific. Most messages are 1-3 sentences of 10-35 words. He goes long only to explain a cause or announce a change, and then he writes paragraphs, not lists.

## This skill overrides chat-style rules

Caveman mode, terse-output rules, and the "no hedging" rule in CLAUDE.md govern how Claude talks to Julian. They do not apply to drafts written as Julian. His real voice uses full sentences, articles, and softeners like "I think" and "Not sure if ...?". Keep them. If a humanizer pass runs afterwards, this skill wins on conflicts.

## Before drafting

Read the examples file for the context you are writing in. Match its length and shape before you match its words.

| Context | Examples file |
|---|---|
| Chat DM or channel | `examples/chat.md` |
| PR review comment or reply | `examples/pr-comments.md` |
| PR title, PR description, commit message | `examples/pr-and-commits.md` |
| GitHub issue or issue comment | `examples/issues.md` |

## After drafting

Once a draft is final and meant to be posted, log it so Julian's later edits can improve this skill. Pass the draft text on stdin:

```bash
uv run ~/.claude/skills/julian-voice/scripts/feedback.py draft --context <context> --target <target>
```

| Context | `--context` | `--target` |
|---|---|---|
| Chat | `chat` | server and channel, or DM partner |
| PR review comment | `pr-comment` | PR URL |
| PR description / title | `pr-description` / `pr-title` | PR URL |
| Commit message | `commit` | absolute path of the local repo |
| Issue comment / new issue | `issue-comment` / `issue` | issue URL, or repo URL for a new issue |

Log one entry per piece of text. A PR title and its description are two entries. When Julian asks to review voice feedback, follow `FEEDBACK.md` in this skill's directory.

## Shape by context

**Chat.** Median 19 words. Lowercase starts and no final period are normal. Casual words are normal: "y'all", "gonna", "cuz", "rq", "iirc", "lol". End with a `:shortcode:` emoji when one fits (`:+1:`, `:joy:`, `:shrug:`, `:facepalm:`). Greet only when opening a conversation or channel post: "Howdy", "Morning y'all,", "Hey team,". Links go on their own line with a one-line description. Times look like "1230 EST".

**PR review comment.** Median 16 words. Pick one of three forms:
- A bare fragment for trivial fixes: "lingering import", "Can be removed", "Use `pytest.approx` instead."
- A lowercase label: `nitpick:`, `suggestion:`, `question:`, followed by a direct sentence and its reason.
- A question for judgment calls: "Would it make sense to ...?", "Is there a way to ...?", "What do you think about ...?", followed by "Mostly asking since ...".

Put code after "something like this:" in an untagged fence. Identifiers go in backticks. Link docs as evidence.

**Replying to review.**
- Accepting: "Good catch, changed." / "Good point." / "Thanks for catching that." plus what you did.
- Your own mistake: "Whoops," / "Shoot," / "my bad" plus the fix in one clause.
- Changing your mind later: "Coming back to this, ..." or "The more I thought about it, ...".
- Pushing back: concede part first ("I agree, but ...", "True, and ..."), then the concrete reason. For a strong position use "I'm going to push against ... because ...".
- Approving: "LGTM, rebase your branch and then I'll approve :thumbsup:".

**PR title.** Check the repo's recent history with `git log` first. If the repo already follows its own format, such as `type(scope): subject` or a leading `(#123)` issue number, use that format. Otherwise the format is `type: subject`.
- **Types:** `feat`, `fix`, `ci`, `chore`, `doc`, `revert`, `test`. A breaking change is `feat!:`.
- **Subject:** a lowercase imperative clause with no trailing period: "feat: give the connector egress to its origins".
- **Joining items:** use ", " ("fix: cap workers at 50 jobs, raise root volume to 50GB, fix the Docker cleanup").
- **Why the title matters:** when the repo squash-merges, the title becomes the commit on the default branch.

The older styles (`KEY-N - Adding ...`, `NOREF - ...`) in `examples/pr-and-commits.md` are history. Use them only when Julian asks for that style.

**PR description.** Median 20 words. Open with the non-obvious fact, the reason, a link ("See <url>"), or "Also ...". The title already says what the PR does, so the description starts where the title stops. For several changes, use `- ` bullets starting with Added/Updated/Removed/Moved/Renamed, or "`identifier` updated from `X` to `Y`". Give each reason inline ("as", "since", "in favor of") or in a nested sub-bullet. Show proof with a short lead line: "Confirmed working here: <workflow run url>", a fenced error, or a captioned screenshot. End after the last fact. Headers appear only in long descriptions, and they name an area ("## Helm Related Changes").

**Commit message.** The subject follows the same format rule as the PR title: the repo's own format when it has one, otherwise `type: subject`. In someone else's repo, copy the owner's convention for the body too, judged from their recent commits in `git log`:
- **Owner writes subject-only commits:** write a subject only, such as `fix(quests): Dragon's Breath farming hint and Trinity Gem boss capture`.
- **Owner writes bodies:** wrap at 80 columns and walk the cause. Open with what is broken ("Without this patch applied, ..."), trace it through exact `Class#method` names, then say what "This patch ..." changes and what stays unaffected. `examples/pr-and-commits.md` has a full example.
- **Repo has no convention:** write one to three short sentences saying why, in his voice.

```
fix: publish releases with an image that has the gh cli

The release job was using an image without gh, so it failed before publishing.
```

**GitHub issue.** Start with "As an engineer, I want to ..." or a plain problem statement. Follow with evidence (error text, workflow run link). Then bold labels on their own lines: `**TASKS:**`, `**AC:**`, `**QA:**`, plus `**REPOS:**` or `**References:**` when useful. Tasks name exact variables, paths, and values. AC are observable outcomes. Small issues can be one or two lines.

**Issue comment.** Open with @mentions when addressing people, with the question on the same line or the next. Status updates are past tense and carry proof: "Deployed to dev: <url>", "Confirmed working in dev after rerunning the previously failed run." Close issues with "Marking as won't do, as ..." or "Implemented with <link>". Put any "cc @Name" line last. No "!" and no emoji.

## Habits across contexts

- **Requests:** "When you get a chance, do you mind ...?" plus why. "Please" is rare.
- **Hedges:** one per message, placed before the claim, followed by the reason. Use "I think", "Not sure if ...?", "I believe", "probably", "imo", or "(could be wrong on this)".
- **Questions:** state your own guess and end with "right?" or "correct?". Ask what someone meant before assuming: "Not sure I follow what you mean by that?"
- **Causes:** "The issue is that ...". Walk the chain step by step, use exact identifiers, and paste the error line.
- **Linkers:** "That way ...", "On top of that, ...", "instead of", "for some reason", "e.g.", "~" for approximate numbers ("~3-5 minutes").
- **Emphasis:** `_underscore_` italics or one word in CAPS ("MUCH", "NOT"). Bold appears only as issue section labels.
- **Humor:** dry, aimed at himself or at the tools, never at the reviewer.

## Swap these for his forms

| Instead of | He writes |
|---|---|
| Em dash, en dash, or semicolon | A comma, a period, or a new sentence |
| "Additionally" / "Furthermore" | "Also" / "On top of that," |
| "i.e." | "e.g." or "for example" |
| "Great question!" / "Thanks for the thorough review!" | Get straight to the answer |
| "Hope this helps" / "Let me know your thoughts!" | Stop after the last fact. Use "Let me know" only when tied to a specific action. |
| `## Summary` / `## Changes` / `**Label:** value` in a PR | Plain bullets or 1-3 sentences |
| Turning a conversational message into a bullet list | Prose. Lists only for truly parallel items. |
| Placeholder sample data (`device-1`) | Realistic values (UUIDs, real timestamps) |
| Literal emoji glyphs | `:shortcode:` |
| "You're absolutely right" | "You are correct," / "Yep you're right." |
| Restating the PR title as the first line | The non-obvious fact, reason, or link |

## Quick prompt

Short, plain, first person. One to three sentences unless explaining a cause. Use the format of the context: lowercase labels in reviews, past-tense proof in issues, -ing titles, commits in the repo owner's format. Soften with "I think" or "Not sure if ...?" and give the reason. Back claims with a link. No em dashes, semicolons, headers in comments, bold outside issue labels, sign-offs, or recaps. Read the matching examples file first.
